sentences.zh: 袁繼鹹，字季通，宜春人。

translations.literal: Yuan Jixian, style name Jitong, was a native of Yichun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jixian, courtesy name Jitong, was from Yichun.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年冬，擢御史，監臨會試，坐縱懷挾舉子，謫南京行人司副，遷主客員外郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Chongzhen he was promoted to censor and supervised the metropolitan examination; for allowing candidates to carry concealed crib notes he was demoted to vice commissioner of the Nanjing Courier Office and later transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Chongzhen year three he was promoted to censor and oversaw the metropolitan examination. Because he had allowed candidates to smuggle in crib notes, he was demoted to vice commissioner of the Nanjing courier service and later made vice director in the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 七年春，擢山西提學僉事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he was promoted to educational intendant of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he was promoted to educational intendant in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 未行，總理戶、工二部中官張彜憲有朝覲官賫冊之奏。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Zhang Yixian, the eunuch supervising the Ministries of Revenue and Works, memorialized that officials attending court audiences should present registers.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, Zhang Yixian, the eunuch in charge of the Ministries of Revenue and Works, memorialized that officials coming to court should submit tribute registers.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹疏論之，謂：「此令行，上自藩臬，下至守令，莫不次第參謁，屏息低眉，跪拜於中官之座，率天下為無恥事，大不便。」

translations.literal: Jixian memorialized against it, saying: "If this order is carried out, from provincial governors and intendants down to prefects and magistrates, none will fail to pay calls in turn, holding their breath and lowering their brows, kneeling and bowing before the eunuch's seat—leading the empire into shamelessness; this is most inexpedient."
translations.idiomatic: Jixian submitted a memorial opposing it, writing: "If this order takes effect, from provincial governors and intendants down to prefects and magistrates, everyone will have to pay calls in succession, breath held and brows lowered, kneeling before a eunuch's seat. The whole empire would be reduced to shamelessness. This would be a grave evil."

sentences.zh: 彜憲大恚，與繼鹹互訐奏。

translations.literal: Yixian was greatly enraged and exchanged impeachment memorials with Jixian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yixian was furious and exchanged impeachment memorials with Jixian.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，乃孑身赴任。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him, and he went alone to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid him no heed, and Jixian went to his post alone.

sentences.zh: 久之，巡撫吳甡薦其廉能。

translations.literal: After some time the grand coordinator Wu Shen recommended his integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: In time Grand Coordinator Wu Shen recommended him for integrity and ability.

sentences.zh: 而巡按御史張孫振以請屬不應，疏誣繼鹹臟私事。

translations.literal: But the touring censor Zhang Sunzhen, because Jixian had not responded to his request for favor, memorialized falsely accusing Jixian of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: But Touring Censor Zhang Sunzhen, whose request for a favor had gone unanswered, memorialized falsely accusing Jixian of graft.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮繼鹹，責甡回奏。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, arrested Jixian, and ordered Shen to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, had Jixian arrested, and ordered Shen to report back.

sentences.zh: 甡賢繼鹹，斥孫振。

translations.literal: Shen praised Jixian and denounced Sunzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen spoke up for Jixian and rebuked Sunzhen.

sentences.zh: 諸生隨至都，伏闕訴冤，繼鹹亦列上孫振請屬狀及其贓賄數事。

translations.literal: Students followed him to the capital, prostrating themselves at the palace gate to plead his innocence; Jixian also submitted Sunzhen's requests for favor and several matters of bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Students followed him to the capital and knelt at the palace gate to plead his case. Jixian also submitted evidence of Sunzhen's solicitations and several counts of bribery.

sentences.zh: 詔逮孫振，坐謫戍；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sunzhen arrested and he was sentenced to banishment;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Sunzhen arrested, and he was banished to military service on the frontier;

sentences.zh: 繼鹹得復官。

translations.literal: Jixian was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: and Jixian was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 十年，除湖廣參議，分守武昌。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed vice commissioner of Huguang and assigned to defend Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made vice commissioner of Huguang with responsibility for defending Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 以兵搗江賊巢興國、大冶山中，擒賊首呂瘦子，降其黨十余人。

translations.literal: With troops he raided the river bandits' lairs in the mountains of Xingguo and Daye, captured the bandit chief Lü Shouzi, and induced more than ten of his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops against river bandit strongholds in the Xingguo and Daye mountains, captured the chief Lü Shouzi, and induced more than ten of his followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 詔兼僉事，分巡武昌、黃州。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve concurrently as intendant, touring Wuchang and Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve concurrently as intendant with jurisdiction over Wuchang and Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 擊退賊老回回、革裏眼等七大部黃陂、黃安，築黃岡城六千余丈。

translations.literal: He repelled the seven great bandit hosts of Lao Huihui, Ge Liyan, and others at Huangpi and Huang'an, and built more than six thousand zhang of wall at Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: He drove back the seven great bandit armies of Lao Huihui, Ge Liyan, and others at Huangpi and Huang'an, and built more than six thousand zhang of wall at Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 十二年，移淮陽，忤中官楊顯名，奏鐫二秩調用。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Huaiyang; he offended the eunuch Yang Xianming and was memorialized for reduction of two ranks and reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Huaiyang. He offended the eunuch Yang Xianming and was reduced two ranks and reassigned.

sentences.zh: 督師楊嗣昌以其知兵，引參軍事。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Sichang, considering him knowledgeable in military affairs, brought him in as military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Sichang, judging him skilled in military matters, took him on as a staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 明年四月擢右僉都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed to pacify and administer Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the fourth month, he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and charged with pacifying Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 未一年，襄陽陷，被逮，戍貴州。

translations.literal: Within a year Xiangyang fell; he was arrested and banished to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Xiangyang fell. He was arrested and exiled to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，廷臣交薦，起故官，總理河北屯政。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year court officials repeatedly recommended him; he was restored to his former office and put in charge of military colonies north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year officials at court repeatedly recommended him. He was restored to his former rank and placed in charge of military colonies north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 未赴，賊逼江西。

translations.literal: Before he departed, bandits pressed upon Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, rebels threatened Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 廷議設重臣總督江西、湖廣、應天、安慶軍務，駐九江。

translations.literal: The court debated appointing a high official to supervise military affairs in Jiangxi, Huguang, Yingtian, and Anqing, stationed at Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided to appoint a senior official to supervise military affairs in Jiangxi, Huguang, Yingtian, and Anqing, with headquarters at Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 擢繼鹹兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史以行。

translations.literal: Jixian was promoted to right vice minister of War and concurrent right vice censor-in-chief and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian was promoted to right vice minister of War with the concurrent rank of right vice censor-in-chief and sent to take command.

sentences.zh: 賊已陷武昌，左良玉擁兵東下。

translations.literal: The bandits had already taken Wuchang, and Zuo Liangyu was leading his army eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already taken Wuchang, and Zuo Liangyu was marching east with his army.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹遇良玉於蕪湖，激以忠義。

translations.literal: Jixian met Liangyu at Wuhu and stirred him with talk of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian met Liangyu at Wuhu and roused him with appeals to loyalty and duty.

sentences.zh: 良玉即還，恢復武昌。

translations.literal: Liangyu at once turned back and recovered Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu turned back at once and recovered Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 廷議呂大器來代，繼鹹仍督屯政。

translations.literal: The court decided that Lü Daqi would replace him, and Jixian was to continue supervising military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that Lü Daqi would replace him while Jixian continued to supervise military colonies.

sentences.zh: 大器、良玉不協，長沙、袁州俱陷，仍推繼鹹代之。

translations.literal: Daqi and Liangyu did not cooperate; Changsha and Yuanzhou both fell, and Jixian was again recommended to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi and Liangyu could not work together. Changsha and Yuanzhou both fell, and the court again turned to Jixian to replace Daqi.

sentences.zh: 甫抵鎮而京師陷。

translations.literal: He had just reached his command when the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely reached his post when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王立南都，頒詔武昌，良玉不拜詔。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu established the Southern Capital and issued an edict at Wuchang; Liangyu would not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu established the Southern Court and issued an edict at Wuchang, Liangyu refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹致書言倫序正，良玉乃拜受詔。

translations.literal: Jixian wrote explaining that the order of succession was correct, and Liangyu then bowed and received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian wrote to explain that the succession was legitimate, and Liangyu then accepted the edict with obeisance.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹入朝，高傑新封興平伯。

translations.literal: Jixian entered court; Gao Jie had just been enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian went to court, where Gao Jie had just been enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 繼咸曰：「封爵以勸有功。

translations.literal: Jixian said: "Titles and fiefs are granted to encourage merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian said: "Titles and fiefs are meant to reward merit.

sentences.zh: 無功而封，有功者不勸。

translations.literal: To enfeoff the meritless does not encourage the meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffing the undeserving will not encourage those who have earned reward.

sentences.zh: 跋扈而封，跋扈愈多。」

translations.literal: To enfeoff the overbearing makes overbearing men more numerous."
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffing the insubordinate will only breed more insubordination."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「事已行，奈何？」

translations.literal: The king said: "The deed is already done—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "The deed is already done. What can be done now?"

sentences.zh: 繼咸曰：「馬士英引傑渡江，宜令往輯。」

translations.literal: Jixian said: "Ma Shiying brought Jie across the Yangzi; he should be ordered to go and pacify the region."
translations.idiomatic: Jixian said: "Ma Shiying brought Jie across the Yangzi. He should be ordered to go and restore order there."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「彼不欲往，輔臣史可法願往。」

translations.literal: The king said: "He does not wish to go; Grand Secretary Shi Kefa is willing to go."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "He does not wish to go. Grand Secretary Shi Kefa is willing to go instead."

sentences.zh: 繼咸曰：「陛下嗣位，固以恩澤收人心，尤宜以紀綱肅眾誌。

translations.literal: Jixian said: "Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne and rightly uses favor to win hearts, but you should all the more use discipline to steady the will of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian said: "Your Majesty has taken the throne and rightly uses favor to win hearts, but you must also use discipline to steady the will of the court.

sentences.zh: 乞振精神，申法紀。

translations.literal: I beg you to rouse your spirit and enforce the law.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to rouse your spirit and enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 冬春間，淮上未必無事。

translations.literal: Between winter and spring there may well be trouble on the Huai front.
translations.idiomatic: Between winter and spring there may well be trouble on the Huai front.

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑，願奉六龍為澶淵之舉。」

translations.literal: Though I am untalented, I am willing to follow the imperial carriage as in the covenant of Chanyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I am willing to follow Your Majesty's carriage as in the covenant of Chanyuan."

sentences.zh: 王有難色。

translations.literal: The king looked troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The prince looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 因詣榻前密奏曰：「左良玉雖無異圖，然所部多降將，非孝子順孫。

translations.literal: He then went before the couch and reported in secret: "Although Zuo Liangyu has no rebellious intent, his troops are mostly surrendered generals—not filial sons or obedient grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the couch and spoke in confidence: "Although Zuo Liangyu has no rebellious intent, his troops are mostly surrendered generals, not men of filial loyalty.

sentences.zh: 陛下初登大寶，人心危疑，意外不可不慮，臣當星馳回鎮。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has just ascended the throne; hearts are anxious and doubtful; the unexpected cannot be left unconsidered. I should hurry back to my command."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has just taken the throne, and hearts are uneasy. The unexpected cannot be ignored. I should ride back to my post at once."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The prince granted his request.

sentences.zh: 因赴閣責可法不當封傑，士英嗛之。

translations.literal: He then went to the Grand Secretariat and reproached Kefa for improperly enfeoffing Jie; Shiying resented this.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the Grand Secretariat and reproached Kefa for improperly enfeoffing Jie. Shiying took offense.

sentences.zh: 俄陳致治守邦大計，引宋高宗用黃潛善、汪伯彥事，語復侵士英。

translations.literal: Soon after he set forth the great plan for governing and defending the realm, citing how Song Gaozong employed Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan—language that again impugned Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he set forth his plan for governing and defending the realm, citing how Emperor Gaozong of Song had employed Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan—language that again struck at Shiying.

sentences.zh: 會湖廣巡按御史黃澍劾奏士英十大罪，士英擬旨逮治。

translations.literal: At the same time Huang Shu, touring censor of Huguang, memorialized ten great crimes of Shiying; Shiying drafted an edict for his arrest.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Huang Shu, touring censor of Huguang, memorialized ten grave charges against Shiying. Shiying drafted an edict for his arrest.

sentences.zh: 澍與良玉謀，陰諷將士大嘩，欲下南京索餉，保救澍。

translations.literal: Shu plotted with Liangyu, secretly inciting the officers and men to raise a great clamor, intending to march on the Southern Capital to demand pay and secure Shu's rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Shu plotted with Liangyu, secretly stirring the troops to mutiny with the aim of marching on Nanjing to demand pay and save Shu.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹為留江漕十萬石、餉十三萬金給之，且代澍申理，以良玉依仗澍為言。

translations.literal: Jixian retained for them one hundred thousand piculs of Yangzi grain transport and one hundred thirty thousand taels of silver in pay, and also pleaded Shu's case on his behalf, citing Liangyu's reliance on Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian set aside one hundred thousand piculs of Yangzi grain transport and one hundred thirty thousand taels in pay for them, pleaded Shu's case, and cited Liangyu's dependence on Shu.

sentences.zh: 士英不得已，免逮澍。

translations.literal: Shiying had no choice but to spare Shu's arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying had no choice but to drop the arrest of Shu.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹既與士英隙，所奏悉停寢。

translations.literal: Once Jixian was at odds with Shiying, all his memorials were left in abeyance.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jixian had fallen out with Shiying, none of his memorials received action.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，繼鹹言：「元朔者，人臣拜手稱觴之日，陛下嘗膽臥薪之時。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Jixian said: "The new year's first day is when ministers bow and raise their cups in congratulation; it should be a time for Your Majesty to taste gall and sleep on brushwood.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Jixian said: "The new year's day is when ministers bow and offer congratulations; it should be a time for Your Majesty to taste gall and sleep on brushwood.

sentences.zh: 念大恥未雪，宜以周宣之未央問夜為可法，以晚近長夜之飲、角之戲為可戒。

translations.literal: Remembering that great shame is not yet washed away, you should take King Xuan of Zhou's vigil at Weiyang as a model, and take recent all-night drinking and sumo contests as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Great shame is not yet avenged. You should take King Xuan of Zhou's midnight vigil at Weiyang as your model, and regard recent all-night revelry and wrestling games as warnings.

sentences.zh: 省土木之功，節浮淫之費。

translations.literal: Reduce works of earth and wood; curtail extravagant and licentious expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Cut back construction projects and curb wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 戒諭臣工，後私鬥而急公仇。

translations.literal: Admonish the officials to put private quarrels last and public enmity first.
translations.idiomatic: Admonish your ministers to set aside private quarrels and unite against the common foe.

sentences.zh: 臣每嘆三十年來，徒以三案葛藤血戰不已。

translations.literal: Your servant often laments that for thirty years men have fought in bloody strife over nothing but the entanglements of the Three Cases.
translations.idiomatic: I often lament that for thirty years men have fought in bloody strife over nothing but the entanglements of the Three Cases.

sentences.zh: 若《要典》一書，已經先帝焚毀，何必復理其說。

translations.literal: As for the book Summaries of Essentials, the late emperor already had it burned—why revisit its doctrines?
translations.idiomatic: The book Summaries of Essentials was already burned by the late emperor. Why revisit its doctrines?

sentences.zh: 書茍未進，宜寢之；

translations.literal: If the book has not yet been submitted, it should be laid aside;
translations.idiomatic: If the book has not yet been submitted, let it lie;

sentences.zh: 即已進，宜毀之。

translations.literal: if it has been submitted, it should be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: if it has been submitted, destroy it.

sentences.zh: 至王者代興，從古亦多異同。

translations.literal: As for the rise of one royal house in place of another, from antiquity there have been many differences and similarities.
translations.idiomatic: When one dynasty succeeds another, history offers many parallels and contrasts.

sentences.zh: 平、勃迎立漢文，不聞窮治朱虛之過；

translations.literal: Chen Ping and Zhou Bo installed Emperor Wen of Han, yet one does not hear that they pursued to the end the faults of the Lü clan;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping and Zhou Bo installed Emperor Wen of Han, yet they did not pursue to the end the crimes of the Lü clan;

sentences.zh: 房、杜決策秦邸，不聞力究魏征之非。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui decided affairs at the Prince of Qin's residence, yet one does not hear that they pressed hard on Wei Zheng's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui decided affairs at the Prince of Qin's residence, yet they did not press hard on Wei Zheng's past errors.

sentences.zh: 固其君豁達大度，亦其大臣公忠善謀，翊贊其美。

translations.literal: Surely their ruler was magnanimous and broad-minded, and their great ministers were loyal, public-spirited, and skilled in counsel, assisting and praising his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: This was because their rulers were magnanimous, and their ministers loyal, public-spirited, and skilled in counsel, assisting and praising their sovereign's virtue.

sentences.zh: 請再下寬大之詔，解圜扉疑入之囚，斷草野株連之案。」

translations.literal: He requested that another edict of clemency be issued, releasing prisoners imprisoned on suspicion behind round prison doors, and closing cases of guilt-by-association in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that another edict of mercy be issued—to free those jailed on mere suspicion and to halt cases that dragged innocent families across the countryside into ruin.

sentences.zh: 王降旨俞其言。

translations.literal: The prince issued a rescript approving his words.
translations.idiomatic: The prince issued an edict granting his request.

sentences.zh: 群小皆不喜繼鹹，汰其軍餉六萬，軍中有怨言，繼鹹疏爭不得。

translations.literal: The petty faction all disliked Jixian; they cut his army pay by sixty thousand, and there was discontent in the army; Jixian memorialized in protest but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The court clique resented Jixian; they slashed his army's pay by sixty thousand taels, sparking muttering in the ranks. Jixian memorialized in protest, but his plea went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 又以江上兵寡，鄭鴻逵戰艦不還，議更造，檄九江僉事葉士彥於江流截買材木。

translations.literal: Also, because troops on the river were few and Zheng Hongkui's warships had not returned, they discussed building new ones and dispatched an order to Ye Shiyan, the Jiujiang intendant, to intercept and purchase timber on the river.
translations.idiomatic: With too few troops on the Yangzi and Zheng Hongkui's warships still absent, the court resolved to build replacements and ordered Ye Shiyan, intendant at Jiujiang, to buy timber cut from the riverbanks.

sentences.zh: 士彥家蕪湖，與諸商昵，封還其檄。

translations.literal: Shiyan's family was in Wuhu; he was on familiar terms with the merchants and returned the dispatch sealed.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan's family was based in Wuhu, where he was on cozy terms with the merchant guilds; he sealed the order and sent it back unopened.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹以令不行，疏劾士彥。

translations.literal: Jixian, because the order was not carried out, memorialized impeaching Shiyan.
translations.idiomatic: When the order went unexecuted, Jixian memorialized the throne to impeach Shiyan.

sentences.zh: 士彥同年御史黃耳鼎亦劾繼鹹，言繼鹹有心腹將校勸左良玉立他宗，良玉不從雲。

translations.literal: Shiyan's fellow metropolitan examination-year censor Huang Erding also impeached Jixian, saying that Jixian had close subordinate officers who urged Zuo Liangyu to establish another imperial lineage, and that Liangyu did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan's examination-year colleague, Censor Huang Erding, also impeached Jixian, alleging that Jixian's trusted officers had urged Zuo Liangyu to put forward a rival claimant to the throne—a proposal Liangyu refused.

sentences.zh: 良玉嘗不拜監國詔，聞之益疑懼，上疏明與繼鹹無隙，耳鼎受指使而言，《要典》宜再焚。

translations.literal: Liangyu had once refused to bow to the regency edict; hearing this he grew more suspicious and fearful, and memorialized clarifying that he had no rift with Jixian, that Erding spoke under instruction, and that the Summaries of Essentials should again be burned.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu, who had once refused to acknowledge the regency edict, grew still more alarmed. He memorialized to declare that he and Jixian were not at odds, that Erding spoke at someone's bidding, and that the Summaries of Essentials ought to be burned once more.

sentences.zh: 江東人乃由是交口言繼鹹、良玉倡和，脅制朝廷矣。

translations.literal: People east of the river then from this spoke with one voice, saying that Jixian and Liangyu were acting in concert and coercing the court.
translations.idiomatic: From that point, voices across the lower Yangzi converged on a single claim: Jixian and Liangyu were working in tandem to intimidate the court.

sentences.zh: 會都下又有偽太子之事，良玉爭不得，遂與士英輩有隙。

translations.literal: Just then there was also in the capital the affair of the false crown prince; Liangyu could not prevail in the dispute, and thus had a rift with Ma Shiying and his faction.
translations.idiomatic: About then the capital was shaken by the case of the supposed crown prince. Liangyu failed to get his way and fell out with Ma Shiying and his allies.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹疏言：「太子真偽，非臣所能懸揣。

translations.literal: Jixian memorialized, saying: "Whether the crown prince is genuine or false is not something your minister can presumptuously judge.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian submitted a memorial: "Whether the crown prince is genuine or an impostor lies beyond this minister's power to decide.

sentences.zh: 真則望行良玉言，偽則不妨從容審處，多召東宮舊臣辨識，以解中外之疑。」

translations.literal: If he is genuine, then I hope Your Majesty will act on Liangyu's words; if false, there is no harm in handling the matter calmly and deliberately, summoning many former eastern-palace officials to identify him, so as to resolve doubts within and without.
translations.idiomatic: If he is real, I would ask that Your Majesty heed Liangyu's counsel. If he is false, the matter can be examined at leisure—summon former officials of the eastern palace to identify him and lay to rest the suspicions of court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 疏未達，良玉已反。

translations.literal: The memorial had not yet arrived when Liangyu had already rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial even reached the capital, Liangyu had already risen in revolt.

sentences.zh: 初，繼鹹聞李自成兵敗南下，命部將郝效忠、陳麟、鄧林奇守九江，自統副將汪碩畫、李士元等援袁州，防賊由岳州、長沙入江西境。

translations.literal: Initially, when Jixian heard that Li Zicheng's army had been defeated and was heading south, he ordered his generals Hao Xiaozhong, Chen Lin, and Deng Linqi to hold Jiujiang, while he personally led the deputy generals Wang Shuohua, Li Shiyuan, and others to relieve Yuanzhou, guarding against bandits entering Jiangxi by way of Yuezhou and Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on hearing that Li Zicheng's forces had been broken and were fleeing south, Jixian ordered Hao Xiaozhong, Chen Lin, and Deng Linqi to hold Jiujiang while he himself marched with Wang Shuohua, Li Shiyuan, and other deputies to relieve Yuanzhou, blocking any rebel advance into Jiangxi through Yuezhou and Changsha.

sentences.zh: 既已登舟，聞良玉反，復還九江。

translations.literal: Having already boarded a boat, upon hearing that Liangyu had rebelled, he returned again to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He had already put to water when word came of Liangyu's rebellion; he turned back at once to Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 良玉舟在北岸，貽書繼鹹，願握手一別，為皇太子死。

translations.literal: Liangyu's boat was on the north bank; he sent a letter to Jixian, wishing to clasp hands once in farewell and die for the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu's fleet lay on the north bank. He wrote to Jixian asking for one final meeting, saying he was ready to die for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 九江士民泣請繼鹹往，紓一方難。

translations.literal: The officials and people of Jiujiang wept and begged Jixian to go, to relieve the crisis of the region.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jiujiang, weeping, pleaded with Jixian to go and spare the city its ordeal.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹會良玉於舟中，良玉語及太子下獄事，大哭。

translations.literal: Jixian met Liangyu on the boat; Liangyu spoke of the crown prince's imprisonment and wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian went aboard to meet Liangyu, who spoke of the crown prince's imprisonment and broke into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 次日，舟移南岸，良玉袖出皇太子密諭，劫諸將盟。

translations.literal: The next day the boat moved to the south bank; Liangyu pulled from his sleeve a secret edict from the crown prince and forced the generals to swear an oath.
translations.idiomatic: The following day the vessel crossed to the south bank. Liangyu produced from his sleeve a secret order purportedly from the crown prince and compelled his officers to swear allegiance to it.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹正色曰：「密諭何從來？

translations.literal: Jixian said sternly: "Whence comes this secret edict?
translations.idiomatic: Jixian answered coldly, "Where did this secret edict come from?

sentences.zh: 先帝舊德不可忘，今上新恩亦不可負，密諭何從來？」

translations.literal: The former emperor's old kindness must not be forgotten; the present sovereign's new grace also must not be betrayed—whence comes this secret edict?
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's kindness must not be forgotten, and the reigning sovereign's favor must not be cast aside—where did this secret edict come from?

sentences.zh: 良玉色變，良久乃曰：「吾約不破城，改檄為疏，駐軍侯旨。」

translations.literal: Liangyu's countenance changed; after a long while he said: "I promise not to storm the city; I will change my proclamation to a memorial and encamp my army to await imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu's face darkened. At length he said, "I will not assault the city. I shall recast my proclamation as a memorial and hold my troops in camp until I receive the throne's command."

sentences.zh: 繼鹹歸，集諸將於城樓而灑泣曰：「兵諫非正。

translations.literal: Jixian returned, gathered the generals on the city tower, and with tears said: "Military remonstrance is not the proper way.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian returned to the city, assembled his officers on the tower, and said through tears, "To remonstrate with arms is not the right path.

sentences.zh: 晉陽之甲，《春秋》惡之，可同亂乎？」

translations.literal: The raising of arms at Jinyang—the Spring and Autumn Annals condemn it; can we join together in rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin raised troops at Jinyang, the Spring and Autumn Annals marked it as evil. Are we to share in such disorder?

sentences.zh: 遂約與俱拒守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made a pact with them all to refuse submission and hold the defense together.
translations.idiomatic: He then bound them all by oath to stand firm and defend the city together.

sentences.zh: 而效忠及部將張世勛等則已出與良玉合兵，入城殺掠。

translations.literal: But Xiaozhong and the subordinate generals Zhang Shixun and others had already gone out to join forces with Liangyu, entering the city to kill and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hao Xiaozhong, Zhang Shixun, and other officers had already gone over to Liangyu, joined his forces, and entered the city to kill and loot.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹聞之，欲自盡。

translations.literal: When Jixian heard this, he wished to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, Jixian wanted to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 黃澍入署拜泣曰：「寧南無異圖。

translations.literal: Huang Shu entered the office, bowed, and wept, saying: "The Prince of Ningnan harbors no ulterior design.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shu came into the yamen, bowed, and wept. "The Prince of Ningnan has no treacherous intent,

sentences.zh: 公以死激成之，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Lordship uses death to provoke him, the great enterprise will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: but if you die now and goad him into worse, all will be lost.

sentences.zh: 副將李士春亦密白繼鹹隱忍，至前途，王文成之事可圖也。

translations.literal: The deputy general Li Shichun also secretly advised Jixian to forbear, saying that further ahead the affair of Wang Wencheng could still be attempted.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy General Li Shichun also sent a private message urging Jixian to swallow his grief: patience now might yet allow them to accomplish what Wang Wencheng had once done.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹以為然，遂出責良玉。

translations.literal: Jixian thought this reasonable and so went out to reproach Liangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian accepted the counsel and went out to rebuke Liangyu in person.

sentences.zh: 良玉已疾篤，夜望見城中火起，大哭曰：「予負臨侯！」

translations.literal: Liangyu was already gravely ill; at night, seeing fire rise in the city, he wept greatly and said: "I have failed Lord Linhou!
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu was already near death. That night, seeing flames leap up within the city, he sobbed, "I have betrayed Lord Linhou!

sentences.zh: 臨侯，繼鹹別號也。

translations.literal: Linhou was Jixian's style name.
translations.idiomatic: Linhou was Jixian's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 嘔血數升，遂死。

translations.literal: He vomited several sheng of blood and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He coughed up bowl after bowl of blood and died.

sentences.zh: 其子夢庚秘不發喪，諸將推為帥，移舟東。

translations.literal: His son Menggeng kept the death secret without announcing the funeral; the generals pushed him to be commander and moved the boats east.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuo Menggeng concealed the death and withheld the funeral rites. The officers proclaimed him commander and steered the fleet eastward.

sentences.zh: 中朝皆疑繼鹹、良玉同反。

translations.literal: The central court all suspected that Jixian and Liangyu had rebelled together.
translations.idiomatic: At court, many now suspected that Jixian and Liangyu had rebelled in concert.

sentences.zh: 而南都時已破，諸鎮多納款。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Southern Capital had already fallen, and many garrison commanders submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Southern Capital had already fallen, and one garrison after another was surrendering.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹勸夢庚旋師，不聽。

translations.literal: Jixian urged Menggeng to turn the army back, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian pleaded with Menggeng to march his troops home, but Menggeng refused.

sentences.zh: 遣人語林奇、碩畫、士元毋為不忠事，林奇、碩畫、士元避皖湖中，遣人陰逆繼鹹。

translations.literal: He sent men to tell Linqi, Shuohua, and Shiyuan not to do disloyal things; Linqi, Shuohua, and Shiyuan took refuge in the lakes of Wan, sending men secretly to welcome Jixian.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Deng Linqi, Wang Shuohua, and Li Shiyuan not to commit any act of disloyalty. They withdrew into the lakes of Wan and dispatched envoys in secret to receive Jixian.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹已為效忠紿赴其軍。

translations.literal: Jixian had already been deceived by Xiaozhong into going to his army.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian, however, had already been lured by Hao Xiaozhong into joining his camp.

sentences.zh: 將及湖口，而夢庚、效忠降於我大清，遂執繼鹹北去，館內院。

translations.literal: As they were approaching Hukou, Menggeng and Xiaozhong surrendered to Our Great Qing; they then seized Jixian and took him north, lodging him in an inner court residence.
translations.idiomatic: Just before they reached Hukou, Menggeng and Xiaozhong surrendered to Our Great Qing. They seized Jixian and marched him north, housing him in an inner court residence.

sentences.zh: 至明年三月，終不屈，乃殺之。

translations.literal: By the third month of the following year he still would not submit, and they then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the third month of the following year came and he still would not yield, they put him to death.

sentences.zh: 有張亮者，四川人。

translations.literal: There was a Zhang Liang, a native of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Zhang Liang, a man of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his juren degree in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，歷榆林兵備參議，用薦改安廬兵備，監禁軍討賊，頻有功。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he served as military intendant at Yulin; on recommendation he was transferred to An-Lu military intendant, supervised imperial troops in suppressing bandits, and achieved frequent success.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he served as military intendant at Yulin, then, on recommendation, was transferred to the An-Lu command, where he led imperial troops against bandits and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 十七年擢右僉都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of the region.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the reign he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of the territory.

sentences.zh: 福王既立，亮聞李自成兵敗西奔，奏言賊勢可乘，請解職視賊所向，督兵進討，從之。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Fu was established, Liang heard that Li Zicheng's army had been defeated and was fleeing west; he memorialized that the bandit situation could be exploited, requested leave from office to observe where the bandits were heading, and lead troops in pursuit—the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Prince of Fu took the throne, Liang learned that Li Zicheng's army had been broken and was fleeing west. He memorialized that the moment was ripe to strike, asked to leave his post to track the rebels' movements, and offered to lead troops in pursuit. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋召入京議事，復遣還任。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to the capital to discuss affairs, then sent back to his post again.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was called to the capital for consultation, then returned to his command.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，左夢庚陷安慶，亮被執。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year, Zuo Menggeng captured Anqing and Liang was seized.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the fourth month, Zuo Menggeng took Anqing and captured Liang.

sentences.zh: 夢庚北行，挾亮與俱，乘間赴河死。

translations.literal: Menggeng marched north, taking Liang along; Liang seized an opportunity to throw himself into a river and die.
translations.idiomatic: As Menggeng marched north he took Liang with him. Liang found an opening, threw himself into the river, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 申甫者，僧也，好談兵，方私制戰車火器。

translations.literal: Shen Fu was a monk, fond of discussing military matters, and was privately building war chariots and firearms.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Fu was a monk with a passion for military affairs who had been secretly constructing war chariots and gunpowder weapons.

sentences.zh: 帝納聲言，取其車入覽，授都司僉書。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted Sheng's recommendation, took his chariot to inspect, and appointed him staff supervisor registrar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heeded Jin Sheng's recommendation, examined the chariot himself, and appointed Shen Fu registrar in the staff supervisorate.

sentences.zh: 即日召見，奏對稱旨，超擢副總兵，敕募新軍，便宜從事。

translations.literal: That same day he was summoned for audience; his answers pleased the emperor, who promoted him to deputy surveillance commissioner, ordered him to recruit a new army, and granted him discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Fu was summoned the same day. His replies so pleased the emperor that he was abruptly promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner, charged with raising a new army and given full discretion to act.

sentences.zh: 改聲御史，參其軍。

translations.literal: Sheng was reassigned as censor to oversee his army.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng was reassigned as censor to supervise the new force.

sentences.zh: 甫倉猝募數千人，皆市井遊手，所需軍裝戎器又不時給。

translations.literal: Fu hastily recruited several thousand men, all idle town loafers; the required military equipment and weapons were also not supplied in time.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Fu hurriedly raised several thousand men, most of them idle street hands from the markets, while the arms and kit they needed never arrived on schedule.

sentences.zh: 而是時大清兵在郊圻久，勢當速戰，急出營柳林。

translations.literal: But at this time Our Great Qing troops had long been in the suburbs; the situation called for swift battle, so they urgently deployed camp at Willow Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing armies had by then lingered long outside the capital walls, and the moment demanded a quick fight. Shen Fu rushed his men into camp at Willow Grove.

sentences.zh: 總理滿桂節制諸軍，甫不肯為下。

translations.literal: The overall commander Man Gui regulated all the armies, but Fu was unwilling to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Man Gui, the supreme commander, held authority over all forces, but Shen Fu refused to take orders from him.

sentences.zh: 桂卒掠民間，甫軍捕之，桂輒索去。

translations.literal: Gui's soldiers plundered among the people; Fu's army captured them, but Gui repeatedly demanded them back.
translations.idiomatic: Man Gui's troops preyed on the populace; when Shen Fu's men seized them, Man Gui insistently demanded their return.

sentences.zh: 聲以兩軍不和聞，帝即命聲調護。

translations.literal: Sheng reported the discord between the two armies, and the emperor immediately ordered Sheng to mediate.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng reported the feud between the two armies to the throne, and the emperor at once ordered him to reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 亡何，桂歿，甫連敗於柳林、大井，乃結車營盧溝橋。

translations.literal: Before long Man Gui died; Fu suffered successive defeats at Willow Grove and Dajing, then formed a chariot camp at Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Man Gui died. Shen Fu lost battle after battle at Willow Grove and Dajing, then drew up his chariot formation at Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 大清兵繞出其後，禦車者惶懼不能轉，殲戮殆盡，甫亦陣亡。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops circled behind them; those defending the chariots panicked and could not turn them; they were nearly annihilated, and Fu also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing forces swung around to their rear. The charioteers panicked and could not wheel their vehicles about; the unit was cut to pieces, and Shen Fu fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 聲痛傷之，言甫受事日淺，直前沖鋒，遺骸矢刃殆遍，非喋血力戰不至此。

translations.literal: Sheng grieved deeply, saying that Fu had held his post only briefly, yet had charged straight ahead; his remains were nearly covered with arrows and blades—only through bloody, fierce fighting could it have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng mourned him bitterly, saying that Shen Fu had served only a short while yet had led from the front; his body was pierced almost everywhere by arrow and blade—nothing but blood-soaked combat could have brought him to such an end.

sentences.zh: 帝亦傷之，命予恤典。

translations.literal: The emperor also grieved and ordered condolence rites granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved as well and ordered posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 聲恥無功，請率參將董大勝兵七百人，甫遺將古壁兵百人，及豪傑義從數百人，練成一旅，為劉之綸奇兵，收桑榆之效，不許。

translations.literal: Ashamed of his lack of achievement, Sheng requested to lead Deputy General Dong Dasheng's seven hundred troops, the hundred troops of Fu's surviving general Gu Bi, and several hundred heroic volunteer followers, to drill them into one brigade as Liu Zhigang's special strike force and recover something at the eleventh hour—but permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated by his own failure, Jin Sheng asked to take seven hundred men under Dong Dasheng, the hundred survivors led by Gu Bi, and several hundred local volunteers, drill them into a single force, and serve as a flanking strike under Liu Zhigang to snatch victory from defeat. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 俄以清核軍需告竣，奏繳關防，請按律定罪，再疏請罷斥，皆不許。

translations.literal: Soon, as the audit of military supplies was completed, he memorialized returning his official seal, requesting punishment according to law, and again memorialized requesting dismissal—none of this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the audit of army supplies was finished, he submitted his seal and asked to be punished under the law; he memorialized again begging to be dismissed. Both pleas were refused.

sentences.zh: 東江自毛文龍被殺，兵力弱，勢孤。

translations.literal: Since Mao Wenlong was killed, the Eastern Jiang forces had been weak in military strength and isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Mao Wenlong's death, the Eastern Jiang garrison had been understrength and cut off.

sentences.zh: 聲因東宮冊立，自請頒詔朝鮮，俾聯絡東江，張海外形勢。

translations.literal: On the occasion of the eastern palace heir's establishment, Sheng volunteered to promulgate an edict in Korea so as to link up with Eastern Jiang and project strength overseas.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was formally installed, Jin Sheng offered to carry an edict to Korea, reestablish contact with Eastern Jiang, and show the empire's reach beyond the seas.

sentences.zh: 帝雖嘉其意，亦不果用。

translations.literal: Although the emperor praised his intent, it was still not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the idea in principle, but nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 尋上疏言：「陛下曉夜焦勞，日親天下之事，實未嘗日習天下之人。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty toils with worry day and night and daily attends to the affairs of all under Heaven, yet in truth has not daily become familiar with the people of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted a long memorial: "Your Majesty wears yourself thin with care, attending to the business of empire from dawn till midnight, yet you have not truly come to know the men who serve it.

sentences.zh: 必使天下才不才，及才長短，一一程量不爽，方可斟酌位置。

translations.literal: Only by measuring one by one, without error, who under Heaven is talented or not, and the length and shortness of each talent, can posts be carefully assigned.
translations.idiomatic: Only when you have weighed every man's ability—who has talent, who lacks it, and how much each can bear—can you place men where they belong.

sentences.zh: 往者，陛下數召對群臣，問無所得，鮮當聖心，遂厭薄之。

translations.literal: Formerly Your Majesty frequently summoned ministers for audience and questioning, but gained nothing from the questions, rarely hitting the mark with the imperial mind, and thus grew weary and disdained it.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Your Majesty often called ministers in for questioning, yet the sessions yielded little that satisfied you, and you grew tired of them.

sentences.zh: 臣愚妄謂陛下泰交尚未殷，顧問尚未數，不得謂召對無益也。

translations.literal: This foolish minister presumptuously believes that Your Majesty's intimate communion is not yet deep and consultations not yet frequent—it cannot be said that such audiences are useless.
translations.idiomatic: This humble servant dares to think that you have not yet grown close enough to your officials, nor consulted them often enough, to conclude that such audiences serve no purpose.

sentences.zh: 願自今間日禦文華，令京卿、翰林、臺諫及中行、評博等官，輪番入直，博咨廣詢。

translations.literal: I wish that from now on, every other day, Your Majesty would hold court at Wenhua and order capital ministers, Hanlin academicians, censorate officials, and officials such as middle secretaries and evaluation editors to take turns on duty, broadly consulting and widely inquiring.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter, on alternate days, Your Majesty receive audiences in the Wenhua Hall, with ministers of state, Hanlin scholars, censors, and junior officials such as secretaries and evaluation editors serving in rotation, so that counsel may be sought far and wide.

sentences.zh: 而內外有職業者，亦得不時進見。

translations.literal: And those within and without who have specialized expertise may also gain admission to audience from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Men of proven skill, whether inside the capital or beyond it, should also be allowed to come forward when needed.

sentences.zh: 政事得失，軍民利病，廟堂舉錯，邊塞情形，皆與臣工考究於燕閑之間。

translations.literal: Successes and failures in government, benefits and harms to army and people, the court's actions, and frontier conditions—all may be examined together with officials in leisure moments.
translations.idiomatic: In quiet hours you could then examine with your officials what policies succeed and fail, what burdens the people and the army, what the court does amiss, and what the frontiers require.

sentences.zh: 歲月既久，品量畢呈。

translations.literal: As months and years pass, evaluations will all be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Given time, every man's measure would become clear.

sentences.zh: 諸臣才不才，及才長短，豈得逃聖鑒。」

translations.literal: Whether officials are talented or not, and the measure of their talents—how could they escape the sage scrutiny?
translations.idiomatic: Who is fit for office and who is not—none could hide from Your Majesty's discerning eye.

sentences.zh: 帝未及報，聲再疏懇言之，終不用，遂屢疏乞歸。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet replied when Sheng memorialized again earnestly; in the end it was not adopted, and he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before the throne could answer, Jin Sheng wrote again with greater urgency. When his plan was rejected, he began sending memorial after memorial asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 後大學士徐光啟薦聲同修歷書，辭不就。

translations.literal: Later Grand Secretary Xu Guangqi recommended Sheng to jointly compile the calendar, but he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xu Guangqi, the grand secretary, recommended him to help revise the calendar; he declined.

sentences.zh: 以御史召，亦不赴。

translations.literal: When he was summoned as censor, he also did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the court summoned him to serve as censor, he again refused to come.

sentences.zh: 八年春，起山東僉事，復兩疏力辭。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he was raised to Shandong assistant commissioner, but again he twice memorialized forcefully declining.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he was recalled as assistant commissioner in Shandong, and twice submitted firm refusals.

sentences.zh: 鄉郡多盜，聲團練義勇，為捍禦。

translations.literal: His home district had many bandits; Sheng organized militia volunteers for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in his native region, and Jin Sheng raised local militia to defend it.

sentences.zh: 十六年，鳳陽總督馬士英遣使者李章玉征貴州兵討賊，迂道掠江西，為樂平吏民所拒擊。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Fengyang Grand Coordinator Ma Shiying dispatched the envoy Li Zhangyu to raise Guizhou troops to suppress bandits; they took a detour plundering Jiangxi and were repulsed by the officials and people of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Ma Shiying, grand coordinator of Fengyang, sent Li Zhangyu to levy Guizhou troops against the bandits. The column detoured through Jiangxi, looting as it went, and was driven off by the people of Leping.

sentences.zh: 比抵徽州境，吏民以為賊，率眾破走之。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Huizhou territory, the officials and people took them for bandits and led crowds to rout them.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered Huizhou, the local officials and populace mistook them for raiders and mustered in force to break and scatter them.

sentences.zh: 章玉諱激變，謂聲及徽州推官吳翔風主使。

translations.literal: Zhangyu concealed the provocation and claimed that Sheng and the Huizhou push official Wu Xiangfeng had instigated it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangyu hid the fact that his men had provoked the clash and accused Jin Sheng and Wu Xiangfeng, the Huizhou magistrate's assistant, of masterminding the attack.

sentences.zh: 士英以聞，聲兩疏陳辨。

translations.literal: Shiying reported this, and Sheng twice memorialized to explain and defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying relayed the accusation to court; Jin Sheng answered with two memorials in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 帝察其無罪，不問。

translations.literal: The emperor saw that he was guiltless and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found him innocent and took no action.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，廷臣交薦，即命召用，促入都陛見，未赴而京師陷。

translations.literal: That winter, court officials jointly recommended him; he was immediately ordered summoned to service and urged to enter the capital for audience, but before he arrived the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: That winter officials across the court recommended him en masse, and he was ordered at once to take office and hurry to the capital for audience. He never arrived: the city fell first.

sentences.zh: 福王立於南京，超擢聲左僉都御史，聲堅不起。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu was established in Nanjing and extraordinarily promoted Sheng to left vice censor-in-chief, but Sheng firmly refused to take office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu established his court at Nanjing, he elevated Jin Sheng to left vice censor-in-chief in a special appointment. Jin Sheng steadfastly refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 大清兵破南京，列郡望風迎降。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops captured Nanjing, and prefecture after prefecture surrendered at the mere rumor.
translations.idiomatic: After Our Great Qing armies took Nanjing, county after county surrendered at the first rumor of their approach.

sentences.zh: 聲糾集士民保績溪、黃山，分兵扼六嶺。

translations.literal: Sheng rallied gentry and people to defend Jixi and Huangshan, dividing troops to hold the Six Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng gathered local gentry and commoners to hold Jixi and Huangshan, posting troops to guard the six mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 寧國丘祖德、徽州溫璜、貴池吳應箕等多應之。

translations.literal: Qiu Zude of Ningguo, Wen Huang of Huizhou, Wu Yingji of Guichi, and many others largely responded.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zude of Ningguo, Wen Huang of Huizhou, Wu Yingji of Guichi, and others rallied to his call.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使通表唐王，授聲右都御史兼兵部右侍郎，總督諸道軍。

translations.literal: They then sent envoys with a petition to the Tang Prince, who appointed Sheng right censor-in-chief and concurrent right vice minister of War, grand coordinator of all route armies.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to declare allegiance to the Tang Prince, who appointed Jin Sheng right censor-in-chief and concurrent vice minister of War, with overall command of the allied armies.

sentences.zh: 拔旌德、寧國諸縣。

translations.literal: They captured Jingde, Ningguo, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered Jingde, Ningguo, and several neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 九月下旬，徽故御史黃澍降於大清，王師間道襲破之。

translations.literal: In late September, the former Huizhou censor Huang Shu surrendered to Our Great Qing; the royal army by a hidden route launched a surprise attack and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In late ninth month Huang Shu, formerly a Huizhou censor, went over to the Qing side. Imperial troops took a concealed route and struck the loyalist camp by surprise, shattering it.

sentences.zh: 聲被執至江寧，語門人江天一曰：「子有老母，不可死。」

translations.literal: Sheng was captured and taken to Jiangning; he told his disciple Jiang Tianyi: "You have an old mother—you must not die.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng was taken to Jiangning in captivity. He told his student Jiang Tianyi, "Your mother is still alive. You must not die with me.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天一同公起兵，可不同公殉義乎！」

translations.literal: Tianyi replied: "Tianyi rose in arms together with you—how can I not die in loyalty together with you!
translations.idiomatic: Tianyi answered, "I took up arms when you did. How can I fall short of sharing your fate?"

sentences.zh: 遂偕死。

translations.literal: Thereupon they died together.
translations.idiomatic: And so they died together.

sentences.zh: 唐王贈聲禮部尚書，謚文毅。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince posthumously granted Sheng the title Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince posthumously honored him as Minister of Rites, with the temple name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 天一，歙諸生。

translations.literal: Tianyi was a licentiate of She.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tianyi had been a student of She county.

sentences.zh: 丘祖德，字念修，成都人。

translations.literal: Qiu Zude, styled Nianxiu, was a man of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zude, courtesy name Nianxiu, was a native of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the tenth year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 授寧國推官，以才調濟南。

translations.literal: He was appointed pushi of Ningguo; for talent he was transferred to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed investigating magistrate of Ningguo, he was soon transferred to Jinan on account of his ability.

sentences.zh: 用薦超擢僉事，分巡東昌。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was promoted out of turn to vice commissioner, with divided duty touring Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for exceptional merit, he was promoted out of turn to vice commissioner and assigned to tour and pacify Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 山東土寇猖獗，帝因給事中張元始言，令祖德及東兗道李恪專任招撫，寇多解散。

translations.literal: Shandong bandits were rampant; the Emperor, on the words of supervising secretary Zhang Yuanshi, ordered Zude and Li Ke of the East Yan circuit to devote themselves solely to winning them over by grace; many bands dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: With bandits ravaging Shandong, the Emperor—acting on a memorial from supervising secretary Zhang Yuanshi—charged Zude and Li Ke of the East Yan circuit with the sole task of winning the rebels over by conciliation; many bands then broke up and went home.

sentences.zh: 十五年調官沂州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to an office at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was reassigned to a post at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其冬用兵部尚書張國維薦，擢右僉都御史，巡撫保定。

translations.literal: That winter, on Minister of War Zhang Guowei's recommendation, he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the recommendation of Minister of War Zhang Guowei, he was elevated to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 十六年罣察典，解職侯勘。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was implicated in an inspection irregularity, relieved of office, and held pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was caught up in an irregularity during the grand inspection, stripped of his post, and held awaiting investigation.

sentences.zh: 事白，以故官代王永吉撫山東。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared, he resumed his former rank, replacing Wang Yongji as coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Once exonerated, he was restored to his former rank and sent to replace Wang Yongji as Grand Coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 京師覆，賊遣使招降。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, the rebels sent envoys to summon surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, the rebels sent envoys offering terms of surrender.

sentences.zh: 祖德斬之，謀發兵拒守。

translations.literal: Zude beheaded them and plotted to raise troops to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Zude had the envoys executed and set about raising troops to hold the province.

sentences.zh: 會中軍梅應元叛，率部卒索印，祖德乃南奔。

translations.literal: Just then middle-army officer Mei Yingyuan rebelled; leading his soldiers he demanded the seal, and Zude fled south.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Mei Yingyuan, commander of the middle army, mutinied; his troops demanded the official seal, and Zude fled south.

sentences.zh: 福王時，御史沈宸荃劾祖德及河南總督黃希憲輕棄封疆，詔削籍提訊，久之獲釋。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, censor Shen Chenquan impeached Zude and Henan Grand Coordinator Huang Xixian for lightly abandoning their territory; an edict stripped them of rank and ordered them taken for interrogation; after long detention they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, censor Shen Chenquan impeached Zude and Grand Coordinator Huang Xixian of Henan for abandoning their posts lightly; an edict struck them from the rolls and ordered them brought up for trial. After long imprisonment they were released.

sentences.zh: 而成都亦陷，無家可歸，流寓寧國。

translations.literal: Chengdu too had fallen; with no home to return to, he drifted to Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu had also fallen; with nowhere to return, he took refuge in Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 金聲起兵績溪，祖德與寧國舉人錢文龍，諸生麻三衡、沈壽蕘等各舉兵應之。

translations.literal: When Jin Sheng raised troops at Jixi, Zude together with Ningguo juren Qian Wenlong and students Ma Sanheng and Shen Shourao each raised forces in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Sheng raised the banner at Jixi, Zude joined with the Ningguo juren Qian Wenlong and the students Ma Sanheng and Shen Shourao, each of them mustering troops in reply.

sentences.zh: 時郡城已失，祖德駐華陽，三衡駐稽亭，他蜂起者又十余部，約共攻郡城。

translations.literal: By then the prefectural city was already lost; Zude encamped at Huayang, Sanheng at Jiting, and more than ten other bands that had sprung up likewise agreed to join in assaulting the prefectural city together.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural seat was already lost. Zude held Huayang, Sanheng held Jiting, and more than ten other bands that had risen nearby pledged to assault the city together.

sentences.zh: 不克，壽蕘陣歿，祖德退還山中。

translations.literal: They did not succeed; Shourao fell in battle, and Zude withdrew into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The attack failed. Shourao fell on the field; Zude withdrew into the hills.

sentences.zh: 大清兵攻拔其寨，被獲，磔死，其子亦死。

translations.literal: Great Qing troops stormed and took his stockade; he was captured and put to death by dismemberment, and his son also died.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing forces stormed his stronghold. Taken alive, he was executed by dismemberment; his son died as well.

sentences.zh: 越四日，三衡軍敗，亦死。

translations.literal: Four days later Sanheng's army was defeated, and he too died.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later Sanheng's force was broken, and he too perished.

sentences.zh: 壽蕘，都督有容子。

translations.literal: Shourao was the son of regional commander Yourong.
translations.idiomatic: Shourao was the son of the regional commander Yourong.

sentences.zh: 三衡，布政使溶孫也。

translations.literal: Sanheng was the grandson of provincial administration commissioner Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Sanheng was the grandson of the provincial administration commissioner Rong.

sentences.zh: 三衡兵既起，旁近吳太平、阮恒、阮善長、劉鼎甲、胡天球、馮百家與俱起，號七家軍，皆諸生也。

translations.literal: When Sanheng's forces rose, nearby Wu Taiping, Ruan Heng, Ruan Shanchang, Liu Dingjia, Hu Tianqiu, and Feng Baijia rose with him; they were called the Seven Households Army—all were students.
translations.idiomatic: When Sanheng took up arms, Wu Taiping, Ruan Heng, Ruan Shanchang, Liu Dingjia, Hu Tianqiu, and Feng Baijia of the neighboring districts rose with him. They styled themselves the Seven Households Army—all of them were students.

sentences.zh: 三衡既敗，太平等亦死。

translations.literal: After Sanheng was defeated, Taiping and the others also died.
translations.idiomatic: After Sanheng's defeat, Taiping and the rest likewise died.

sentences.zh: 溫璜，初名以介，字於石，烏程人。

translations.literal: Wen Huang, originally named Yijie, styled Yushi, was a man of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Huang, born Yijie and styled Yushi, came from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 大學士體仁再從弟也。

translations.literal: He was a third cousin of Grand Secretary Ti Ren.
translations.idiomatic: He was a third cousin of Grand Secretary Wen Ti Ren.

sentences.zh: 母陸守節被旌。

translations.literal: His mother Lu Shoujie had been honored for chastity.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lu Shoujie, had been publicly honored for her steadfast chastity.

sentences.zh: 璜久為諸生，有學行。

translations.literal: Huang had long been a student, with learning and conduct of note.
translations.idiomatic: Huang had long been a licentiate, renowned for learning and upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年秋舉進士。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examinations and became jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examinations and received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 授徽州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed pushi of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 甫蒞任，聞京師陷，亟練民兵，為保障計。

translations.literal: He had scarcely taken up his post when he heard the capital had fallen; he immediately drilled militia as a plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he assumed his post when word came that the capital had fallen. He at once drilled the militia and laid plans for local defense.

sentences.zh: 明年，南京亦覆。

translations.literal: The next year Nanjing too fell.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Nanjing fell as well.

sentences.zh: 知府秦祖襄及諸僚屬皆遁，璜乃盡攝其印，召士民慰諭之。

translations.literal: Prefect Qin Zuxiang and the other officials all fled; Huang then gathered all their seals, summoned the gentry and commoners, and addressed them with reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Qin Zuxiang and the rest of the official staff fled. Huang collected their seals, summoned gentry and townspeople, and spoke to them words of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 金聲舉兵績溪，璜與掎角，且轉餉給其軍，而徙家屬於村民舍。

translations.literal: When Jin Sheng raised troops at Jixi, Huang coordinated with him in pincer fashion and moreover forwarded provisions to his army, while moving his family to a villager's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Sheng raised troops at Jixi, Huang coordinated with him in a pincer and kept his army supplied, while sending his own family to lodge with villagers.

sentences.zh: 未幾，聲敗，璜嚴兵自守。

translations.literal: Before long Jin Sheng was defeated; Huang kept his troops under strict discipline and held his ground.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jin Sheng was defeated. Huang tightened discipline among his troops and held his position.

sentences.zh: 郡中故御史黃澍以城獻，璜趨歸村舍，刃其妻茅氏及長女，遂自剄死。

translations.literal: The former censor of the prefecture Huang Shu surrendered the city; Huang rushed back to the village dwelling, cut down his wife Lady Mao and his elder daughter, and then cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: The former censor Huang Shu surrendered the city. Huang hurried back to the village house, killed his wife Lady Mao and his elder daughter, then cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 吳應箕，字次尾，貴池人。

translations.literal: Wu Yingji, styled Ciwie, was a man of Guichi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yingji, courtesy name Ciwie, was a native of Guichi.

sentences.zh: 善今古文，意氣橫厲一世。

translations.literal: He excelled in modern and ancient prose; his spirit and ambition swept the age.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in both classical and contemporary prose, and carried himself with a fierce, world-striding pride.

sentences.zh: 阮大鋮以附珰削籍，僑居南京，聯絡南北附珰失職諸人，劫持當道。

translations.literal: Ruan Dacheng, stripped of rank for siding with the eunuch faction, resided in Nanjing and connected north and south with others of the eunuch faction who had lost office, coercing those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Dacheng, stripped of rank for his ties to the eunuch faction, lived in Nanjing and knit together a network of disgraced eunuch partisans from north and south, bullying those who held power.

sentences.zh: 應箕與無錫顧杲、桐城左國材、蕪湖沈士柱、餘姚黃宗羲、長洲楊廷樞等為《留都防亂公揭》討之，列名者百四十余人，皆復社諸生也。

translations.literal: Yingji with Gu Gao of Wuxi, Zuo Guocai of Tongcheng, Shen Shizhu of Wuhu, Huang Zongxi of Yuyao, Yang Tinghu of Changzhou, and others drew up the Public Manifesto to Guard the Southern Capital against Disorder denouncing him; more than a hundred forty signed their names—all were members of the Fushe.
translations.idiomatic: Yingji joined Gu Gao of Wuxi, Zuo Guocai of Tongcheng, Shen Shizhu of Wuhu, Huang Zongxi of Yuyao, Yang Tinghu of Changzhou, and others in issuing the Public Manifesto to Guard the Southern Capital against Disorder, denouncing Ruan. More than a hundred and forty men signed—every one of them a member of the Fushe literary society.

sentences.zh: 後大鋮得誌，謀殺周鑣，應箕獨入獄護視。

translations.literal: Later, when Dacheng gained his aims, he plotted to kill Zhou Biao; Yingji alone entered the prison to watch over and protect him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Dacheng at last got his way, he plotted to kill Zhou Biao. Yingji alone entered the prison to stand watch over him.

sentences.zh: 大鋮聞，急遣騎捕之，應箕夜亡去。

translations.literal: Dacheng heard of it and urgently dispatched riders to capture him; Yingji fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng heard of it and sent horsemen in haste to seize him; Yingji escaped by night.

sentences.zh: 南都不守，起兵應金聲，敗走山中，被獲，慷慨就死。

translations.literal: When the southern capital could not be held, he raised troops in response to Jin Sheng; defeated, he fled into the mountains, was captured, and met death with a generous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern capital could no longer be held, he took up arms in answer to Jin Sheng. Routed, he fled into the mountains, was captured, and went to his death without flinching.

sentences.zh: 其同時舉兵者有尹民興、吳漢超、龐昌胤、謝球、司石磐、王湛、魯之玙。

translations.literal: Those who raised troops at the same time included Yin Minxing, Wu Hanchao, Pang Changyin, Xie Qiu, Si Shipan, Wang Zhan, and Lu Zhiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Others who rose in arms at the same time included Yin Minxing, Wu Hanchao, Pang Changyin, Xie Qiu, Si Shipan, Wang Zhan, and Lu Zhiyu.

sentences.zh: 民興，字宣子，崇禎初舉進士。

translations.literal: Minxing, styled Xuanzi, passed the jinshi in the early Chongzhen period.
translations.idiomatic: Minxing, courtesy name Xuanzi, received his jinshi degree early in the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知寧國、涇二縣，除奸厘蠹，有神明之稱。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Ningguo and Jing counties, eliminating wicked men and rooting out corruption, and was styled a clear-spirited official.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Ningguo and Jing, rooting out villains and clearing away corruption, and won a reputation as an incorruptible, clear-sighted magistrate.

sentences.zh: 行取入都，為陳啟新所訐，謫福建按察司檢校。

translations.literal: Selected for transfer to the capital, he was denounced by Chen Qixin and demoted to inspector of the Fujian surveillance commission.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for appointment in the capital, he was denounced by Chen Qixin and demoted to inspector of the Fujian surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，疏陳時務十四事，帝喜，召為職方主事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year he memorialized fourteen matters of the times; the Emperor was pleased and summoned him as a director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifteenth year he submitted a memorial setting forth fourteen urgent matters of state. The Emperor was pleased and summoned him to serve as a director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 數召對，言多當帝意，即擢本司郎中。

translations.literal: Summoned repeatedly for audience, his words mostly accorded with the Emperor's intent, and he was immediately promoted to director of that bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Called repeatedly to audience, his counsel mostly struck the Emperor's mind, and he was promptly promoted to director of that bureau.

sentences.zh: 周延儒出督師，命從軍贊畫。

translations.literal: When Zhou Yanru went out as grand commander, Minxing was ordered to join the army as strategic planner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yanru went out as grand commander, Minxing was ordered to accompany the army as strategic planner.

sentences.zh: 延儒被譴，下民興吏，除名，久之始釋。

translations.literal: When Yanru was censured, Minxing was handed over to the judicial authorities, struck from the rolls, and only after long time was he released.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanru fell under censure, Minxing was handed over to the judicial authorities, struck from the rolls, and was not released until long afterward.

sentences.zh: 福王立，起故官，尋謝病歸，流寓涇縣。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Minxing was restored to his former office; soon he pleaded illness and retired, drifting to Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Minxing was restored to his former post; soon he pleaded illness and withdrew, taking refuge in Jing County.

sentences.zh: 南京失，與諸生趙初浣等據城拒守，大清兵攻破城，初浣死之，民興走免。

translations.literal: When Nanjing fell, he with student Zhao Chuhuan and others held the city and resisted; Great Qing troops broke the city; Chuhuan died for the cause, and Minxing escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell, he and the student Zhao Chuhuan and others held the city in defense. Our Great Qing forces broke through the walls; Chuhuan died in the fighting, and Minxing escaped.

sentences.zh: 唐王以為御史，事敗歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince appointed him censor; when the cause failed he returned home and died in his house.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince appointed him censor. When that cause collapsed he returned home and died there.

sentences.zh: 漢超，宣城諸生。

translations.literal: Hanchao was a student of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchao was a licentiate of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十七年聞都城變，謀募兵赴難，會福王立，乃已。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, hearing of the disaster at the capital, he plotted to raise troops to rush to the crisis; when the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, on hearing of the catastrophe at the capital, he planned to raise troops and hurry to the rescue; when the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he held back.

sentences.zh: 明年，南都覆，棄家走涇縣，從尹民興起兵。

translations.literal: The next year, when the southern capital fell, he abandoned his family and fled to Jing County, joining Yin Minxing in raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the southern capital fell, he abandoned his household and fled to Jing County, where he joined Yin Minxing in raising troops.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，匿華陽山中。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; he hid in the Huayang mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was broken, he hid in the Huayang hills.

sentences.zh: 先是，丘祖德、麻三衡諸軍潰，保華陽，有徐淮者部署之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the armies of Qiu Zude, Ma Sanheng, and others had been routed and were holding Huayang; one Xu Huai deployed them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the shattered forces of Qiu Zude, Ma Sanheng, and others had fallen back on Huayang, where a man named Xu Huai organized them.

sentences.zh: 漢超與合，連取句容、溧水、高淳、溧陽、涇、太平諸縣。

translations.literal: Hanchao joined with them and in succession took Jurong, Lishui, Gaochun, Liyang, Jing, and Taiping counties.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchao joined them and in succession recovered Jurong, Lishui, Gaochun, Liyang, Jing, and Taiping.

sentences.zh: 明年正月襲寧國，夜緣南城登。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year they raided Ningguo, scaling the south wall by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year they struck at Ningguo, scaling the south wall under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 兵潰，城中按首事者。

translations.literal: The troops were routed; within the city they sought the ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: The force was routed. Inside the city they searched for the ringleader.

sentences.zh: 漢超已出城，念母在，且恐累族人，入見曰：「首事者我也。」

translations.literal: Hanchao had already left the city, but thinking of his mother present and fearing to implicate his clansmen, he entered and said, "I am the one who started this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchao had already slipped out of the city, but his mother was still within, and he feared his clansmen would be implicated. He went back in and said, "I am the one who started this.

sentences.zh: 剖其腹，膽長三寸。

translations.literal: They cut open his belly; his gall bladder was three inches long.
translations.idiomatic: They cut open his belly; his gall bladder measured three inches.

sentences.zh: 妻戚自擲樓下死。

translations.literal: His wife Qi threw herself from a tower to her death.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Qi threw herself from a tower and died.

sentences.zh: 昌胤，西充人。

translations.literal: Changyin was a native of Xichong.
translations.idiomatic: Changyin came from Xichong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he passed the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the tenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授青陽知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 南京覆，走匿九華山，謀舉兵。

translations.literal: When Nanjing fell, he fled and hid on Mount Jiuhua, plotting to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell, he fled and hid on Mount Jiuhua, plotting to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 事泄被執，夜死旅店中。

translations.literal: When the affair leaked he was seized and died in an inn that night.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked out he was seized and died that night in a roadside inn.

sentences.zh: 球，溧陽諸生，僉事鼎新子也。

translations.literal: Qiu was a student of Liyang and the son of the vice commissioner Dingxin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was a licentiate of Liyang and the son of vice commissioner Xie Dingxin.

sentences.zh: 毀家募兵。

translations.literal: He ruined his family's fortune to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his family's entire fortune to raise an army.

sentences.zh: 兵散，被執而死。

translations.literal: When the troops dispersed he was seized and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his force broke up he was captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 石磐，鹽城諸生，與都司酆某同舉兵，兵敗被執。

translations.literal: Shipan, a student of Yancheng, raised troops together with regional commander Feng; when defeated they were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shipan, a licentiate of Yancheng, rose in arms together with the regional commander Feng; when defeated, both were taken.

sentences.zh: 酆言：「此儒生，吾劫之為書記耳。」

translations.literal: Feng said, "This is a scholar—I seized him only to serve as a secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said, "He is only a scholar—I forced him to serve as my secretary.

sentences.zh: 石磐曰：「吾首事，奈何諱之！」

translations.literal: Shipan said, "I was the one who started it—how can you deny it!"
translations.idiomatic: Shipan cried, "I was the ringleader—how dare you deny it!"

sentences.zh: 系獄六十余日，與酆偕死。

translations.literal: Imprisoned more than sixty days, he died together with Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Held in prison for more than sixty days, he died together with Feng.

sentences.zh: 湛，太倉諸生。

translations.literal: Zhan was a student of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was a licentiate of Taicang.

sentences.zh: 城已下，與兄淳復集裏人數百圍城。

translations.literal: After the city had fallen, he together with his elder brother Chun again gathered several hundred neighbors to surround the city.
translations.idiomatic: After the city had fallen, he and his elder brother Chun rallied several hundred neighbors and besieged it anew.

sentences.zh: 城中兵出擊，淳赴水死，湛被斫死。

translations.literal: Soldiers sallied from within; Chun threw himself into the water and died, and Zhan was hacked to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers sallied out against them. Chun drowned himself; Zhan was cut down.

sentences.zh: 之玙，歷官副總兵，駐福山。

translations.literal: Zhiyu had served to deputy regional commander and was stationed at Fushan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu had risen to deputy regional commander and was stationed at Fushan.

sentences.zh: 蘇州既降，諸生陸世鑰聚眾焚城樓。

translations.literal: After Suzhou had surrendered, student Lu Shiyao gathered a crowd and burned the city tower.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzhou surrendered, the student Lu Shiyao gathered a crowd and set fire to the city tower.

sentences.zh: 之玙率千人入城，與大清兵戰，潰走，之玙戰死。

translations.literal: Zhiyu led a thousand men into the city and fought Great Qing troops; routed in flight, Zhiyu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu led a thousand men into the city to fight Our Great Qing forces. Routed, he fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 其時以諸生死者，有六合馬純仁、邳州王臺輔。
