translations.literal: At that time among students who died were Ma Chunren of Liuhe and Wang Taifu of Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Among the students who died at that time were Ma Chunren of Liuhe and Wang Taifu of Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 南京既下，六合即歸附，純仁題銘橋柱，抱石投水死。

translations.literal: After Nanjing fell, Liuhe immediately submitted; Chunren inscribed an epitaph on a bridge pillar and, embracing a stone, threw himself into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing fell, Liuhe submitted at once. Chunren carved an epitaph on a bridge pillar, clasped a stone to his breast, and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 臺輔，當崇禎末，聞宦官復出鎮，將草疏極諫。

translations.literal: Taifu, toward the end of Chongzhen, hearing that eunuchs were again to be sent out to command garrisons, was about to draft a memorial remonstrating to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Taifu, near the end of the Chongzhen reign, heard that eunuchs were to be sent out again to command garrisons and prepared a memorial of the strongest remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 甫入都，都城陷，乃還。

translations.literal: He had just entered the capital when the capital fell, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely reached the capital when it fell, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 福王時，東平伯劉澤清、御史王燮張樂大宴於睢寧。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, Earl of Dongping Liu Zeqing and censor Wang Xie held a great banquet with music at Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, the Earl of Dongping Liu Zeqing and censor Wang Xie gave a great feast with music at Suining.

sentences.zh: 臺輔衰糸至直入，責之曰：「國破君亡，此公等臥薪嘗膽、食不下咽時，顧置酒大會耶！」

translations.literal: Taifu, come in mourning dress, entered straight in and rebuked them, saying: "The realm is broken and the sovereign lost—this is the time for you gentlemen to sleep on brushwood and taste gall, when food will not pass your throats—yet you hold a great feast with wine!
translations.idiomatic: Taifu arrived in full mourning garb, walked straight in, and rebuked them: "The realm is shattered and the sovereign lost—this is the hour for you to sleep on brushwood and taste gall, when grief should choke every morsel—yet you hold a wine feast!

sentences.zh: 左右欲鞭之，燮曰：「狂生也。」

translations.literal: Those at his side would have flogged him; Wang Xie said, "A mad student."
translations.idiomatic: Those beside them would have had him whipped. Wang Xie said, "A mad student."

sentences.zh: 命引去。

translations.literal: He ordered them to lead Taifu away.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them to lead Taifu out.

sentences.zh: 及南京覆，臺輔視其廩曰：「此吾所樹，盡此死。」

translations.literal: When Nanjing fell, Taifu looked at his granary and said, "This I planted myself—when it is exhausted I shall die.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell, Taifu looked at his granary and said, "I planted this myself. When it is gone, I shall die.

sentences.zh: 明年，粟盡，北面再拜，自縊死。

translations.literal: The next year the grain was spent; facing north he bowed twice and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the grain was spent. He bowed twice toward the north and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 沈猶龍，字雲升，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Shen Youlong, styled Yunsheng, was a man of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youlong, courtesy name Yunsheng, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除鄞縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yin County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yin County.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，征授御史，出為河南副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was called to serve as censor and went out as Henan vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianqi reign he was summoned to serve as censor, then sent out as vice commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，召復故官，進太仆少卿，拜右僉都御史，巡撫福建。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former office, advanced to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and made Grand Coordinator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former rank, promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and made Grand Coordinator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 江西妖賊張普薇等作亂，猶龍遣遊擊黃斌卿協剿，大破之。

translations.literal: The demon bandits Zhang Puwei and others of Jiangxi rebelled; Youlong dispatched mobile corps commander Huang Binqing to assist in suppression and broke them decisively.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer-rebel Zhang Puwei and his confederates rose in Jiangxi. Youlong sent the mobile corps commander Huang Binqing to join the suppression and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 增秩賜金，以憂歸。

translations.literal: His rank was raised and gold bestowed; he retired on bereavement leave.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised and gold was bestowed upon him; he then retired to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督兩廣軍務，兼廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of military affairs in the Two Guang, and concurrently Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was complete, he was appointed Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of military affairs in the Two Guang, with concurrent duty as Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十七年冬，福王召理部事，不就，乞葬親歸。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventeenth year, the Prince of Fu summoned him to manage ministry affairs; he did not accept and requested leave to bury his parent and return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventeenth year, the Prince of Fu summoned Shen Youlong to take charge of ministry affairs. He declined, asking instead for leave to bury his parent and return home.

sentences.zh: 明年，南京失守，列城望風下。

translations.literal: The next year Nanjing fell, and walled cities everywhere surrendered at the mere rumor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Nanjing fell, and city after city surrendered at the first rumor of approach.

sentences.zh: 閏六月，吳淞總兵官吳誌葵自海入江，結水寨於泖湖。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month, Wu Zhikui, regional commander at Wusong, entered the river from the sea and established a water camp at Dahu Lake.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month, Wu Zhikui, regional commander at Wusong, came in from the sea and up the river, establishing a floating camp on Dahu Lake.

sentences.zh: 會總兵官黃蜚擁千艘自無錫至，與合。

translations.literal: Just then regional commander Huang Fei arrived from Wuxi at the head of a thousand vessels, and they joined forces.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Huang Fei, regional commander, arrived from Wuxi with a thousand ships, and the two forces united.

sentences.zh: 猶龍乃偕裏人李待問、章簡等，募壯士數千人守城，與二將相掎角，而參將侯承祖守金山。

translations.literal: Youlong then, together with fellow townsman Li Daiwen, Zhang Jian, and others, recruited several thousand stalwart men to defend the city, forming a pincer with the two generals, while vice commander Hou Chengzu held Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: Youlong then joined with fellow townsmen Li Daiwen, Zhang Jian, and others to raise several thousand stalwart men for the city's defense, coordinating with the two generals in a pincer while vice commander Hou Chengzu held Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 八月，大清兵至，二將敗於春申浦，城遂被圍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Our Great Qing troops arrived; the two generals were defeated at Chunshen Creek, and the city was then besieged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Our Great Qing armies arrived. The two generals were routed at Chunshen Creek, and the city was soon under siege.

sentences.zh: 未幾破，猶龍出走，中矢死。

translations.literal: Before long it was broken; Youlong fled and was struck by an arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city fell. Youlong fled but was struck by an arrow and killed.

sentences.zh: 待問守東門，簡守南門，城破，俱被殺。

translations.literal: Daiwen held the east gate and Jian the south gate; when the city fell both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Daiwen defended the east gate and Jian the south gate; when the walls were breached, both were slain.

sentences.zh: 華亭教諭眭明永題詩明倫堂，投繯死。

translations.literal: Su Mingyong, instructor of Huating, composed a poem in the Hall of Bright Ethics and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Su Mingyong, district instructor of Huating, wrote a poem in the Hall of Bright Ethics and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 諸生戴泓赴池死。

translations.literal: Student Dai Hong drowned himself in a pool.
translations.idiomatic: The student Dai Hong threw himself into a pool and drowned.

sentences.zh: 嘉定舉人傅凝之參誌葵軍事，兵敗，赴水死。

translations.literal: Fu Ningzhi of Jiading, a provincial graduate, served in Zhikui's military staff; when the army was defeated he drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ningzhi, a provincial graduate of Jiading who had joined Zhikui's staff, drowned himself after the army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 大清兵遂攻金山，承祖與子世祿猶固守。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops then attacked Jinshan; Chengzu and his son Shilu still held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing forces then moved against Jinshan, but Chengzu and his son Shilu continued to hold out.

sentences.zh: 城既破，巷戰逾時，世祿中四十矢，被獲，死之。

translations.literal: Once the city was broken they fought in the lanes for a long time; Shilu took forty arrows, was captured, and died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell they fought house to house for hours. Shilu took forty arrows, was taken alive, and died defending the position.

sentences.zh: 承祖亦被獲，說之降，不從，遂被殺。

translations.literal: Chengzu was also captured; they urged him to surrender but he refused and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu was captured as well. They pressed him to surrender; he refused and was executed.

sentences.zh: 誌葵、蜚既敗，執至江陰城下，令說城中人降。

translations.literal: After Zhikui and Fei were defeated they were brought to the foot of Jiangyin city and ordered to persuade the people inside to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhikui and Fei, once defeated, were brought beneath the walls of Jiangyin and ordered to persuade the garrison to surrender.

sentences.zh: 誌葵說之，蜚不語，城迄不下，後皆被殺。

translations.literal: Zhikui did so plead, but Fei said nothing; the city never fell, and afterward both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhikui obeyed and pleaded for surrender; Fei kept silent. The city never yielded, and in the end both were put to death.

sentences.zh: 待問，字存我，崇禎末進士。

translations.literal: Daiwen, styled Cunwo, became a jinshi at the end of the Chongzhen reign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daiwen, courtesy name Cunwo, received his jinshi degree in the final years of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a drafting officer in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 工文章，兼精書法。

translations.literal: Skilled in writing, he was also expert in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in belles-lettres and equally masterful in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 簡，字坤能。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Kunneng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, courtesy name Kunneng.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，官羅源知縣。

translations.literal: Successful at the provincial examinations, he served as magistrate of Luoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the provincial examinations, he served as magistrate of Luoyuan.

sentences.zh: 陳子龍，字臥子，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Chen Zilong, styled Wolzi, was a man of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zilong, courtesy name Wolzi, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 生有異才，工舉子業，兼治詩賦古文，取法魏、晉，駢體尤精妙。

translations.literal: Endowed with unusual talent from birth, he excelled at examination essays and also cultivated poetry, fu, and ancient prose, taking Wei and Jin as models; his parallel prose was especially refined.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted from youth, he mastered the examination essay and also poetry, fu, and ancient prose, modeling himself on Wei and Jin writers; his parallel prose was especially exquisite.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the tenth year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 選紹興推官。

translations.literal: Selected as investigating magistrate of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as investigating magistrate of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 東陽諸生許都者，副使達道孫也。

translations.literal: Xu Du of Dongyang, a student, was grandson of vice commissioner Dadao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Du, a student of Dongyang, was the grandson of vice commissioner Dadao.

sentences.zh: 家富，任俠好施，陰以兵法部勒賓客子弟，思得一當。

translations.literal: His family was wealthy; chivalrous and generous, he secretly drilled guests and client youths by military method, seeking one chance to prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: His family was rich. Bold and open-handed, he quietly drilled his retainers and client youths in military order, waiting for one chance to prove himself.

sentences.zh: 子龍嘗薦諸上官，不用，東陽令以私憾之。

translations.literal: Zilong once recommended him to superiors, but they did not employ him; the magistrate of Dongyang bore him private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong had once recommended him to his superiors, but they did not take him up; the magistrate of Dongyang meanwhile nursed a private grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 適義烏奸人假中貴名招兵事發，都葬母山中，會者萬人。

translations.literal: Just then a rogue in Yiwu, using the name of an imperial eunuch to recruit troops, was exposed; Du was burying his mother in the hills, and ten thousand gathered.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment a schemer in Yiwu was caught recruiting troops under a eunuch's name. Du was burying his mother in the hills, and ten thousand men assembled.

sentences.zh: 或告監司王雄曰：「都反矣。」

translations.literal: Someone told intendant Wang Xiong, "Du has rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported to intendant Wang Xiong, "Du has risen in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 雄遽遣使收捕，都遂反。

translations.literal: Xiong hurriedly sent envoys to seize him, and Du then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong at once sent men to arrest him, and Du thereupon rebelled.

sentences.zh: 旬日間聚眾數萬，連陷東陽、義烏、浦江，遂逼郡城，既而引去。

translations.literal: Within ten days he gathered tens of thousands, in succession captured Dongyang, Yiwu, and Pujiang, then pressed the prefectural city, and afterward withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he mustered tens of thousands, seized Dongyang, Yiwu, and Pujiang in turn, then pressed the prefectural seat before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 巡撫董象恒坐事逮，代者未至，巡按御史左光先以撫標兵，命子龍為監軍討之，稍有俘獲。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Dong Xiangheng was arrested for an offense; his replacement had not arrived; touring censor Zuo Guangxian mustered pacification battalion troops and appointed Zilong army supervisor to suppress them, with some prisoners taken.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Dong Xiangheng had been arrested for an offense and no successor had yet arrived. Touring censor Zuo Guangxian mobilized the pacification battalion and put Zilong in charge as army supervisor to suppress the rebels, with some captives taken.

sentences.zh: 而遊擊蔣若來破其犯郡之兵，都乃率余卒三千保南砦。

translations.literal: But guerrilla commander Jiang Ruolai broke the force that was threatening the prefectural city; Du then led his remaining three thousand men to hold the southern stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Guerrilla commander Jiang Ruolai then routed the column threatening the prefectural city, and Du withdrew with his remaining three thousand men to hold a southern stockade.

sentences.zh: 雄欲撫賊，語子龍曰：「賊聚糧據險，官軍不能仰攻，非曠日不克。

translations.literal: Xiong wished to pacify the bandits and said to Zilong, "The rebels have stored grain and hold the heights; government troops cannot attack uphill; it will not be taken except after many days.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong wanted to win the rebels over by conciliation and told Zilong, "They have stockpiled grain and hold the high ground. Government troops cannot storm uphill positions; the place will not fall except after a long siege.

sentences.zh: 我兵萬人，止五日糧，奈何？」

translations.literal: Our troops are ten thousand, with only five days' grain—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: We have ten thousand men and only five days' rations. What then?

sentences.zh: 子龍曰：「都，舊識也，請往察之。」

translations.literal: Zilong said, "Du is an old acquaintance; I ask to go and investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Zilong replied, "Du is an old acquaintance of mine. Let me go and see for myself."

sentences.zh: 乃單騎入都營，責數其罪，諭令歸降，待以不死。

translations.literal: He then alone rode into Du's camp, reproached and enumerated his crimes, instructed him to return and surrender, and promised he would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Alone he rode into Du's camp, rebuked him at length for his crimes, and urged him to surrender, promising that his life would be spared.

sentences.zh: 遂挾都見雄。

translations.literal: He then took Du with him to see Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought Du out to meet Xiong.

sentences.zh: 復挾都走山中，散遣其眾，而以二百人降。

translations.literal: Again he took Du into the hills, dispersed the followers, and brought two hundred men to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He took Du back into the hills, disbanded the main body, and returned with two hundred men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 光先與東陽令善，竟斬都等六十余人於江滸。

translations.literal: Guangxian was on good terms with the Dongyang magistrate and in the end executed Du and more than sixty others on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian was on friendly terms with the magistrate of Dongyang and in the end had Du and more than sixty others beheaded on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 子龍爭，不能得。

translations.literal: Zilong protested but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong objected strenuously but could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 以定亂功，擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying the rebellion he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in putting down the rebellion he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 命甫下而京師陷，乃事福王於南京。

translations.literal: The order had just been issued when the capital fell; he then served the Prince of Fu at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment had scarcely been issued when the capital fell; he then entered the service of the Prince of Fu at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，言防江之策莫過水師，海舟議不可緩，請專委兵部主事何剛訓練，從之。

translations.literal: That sixth month he argued that among strategies to defend the Yangzi none surpassed the navy; the plan for sea vessels could not be delayed; he asked that training be entrusted solely to Ministry of War clerk He Gang—and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month he argued that no Yangzi defense could succeed without a strong navy, that the plan for a sea fleet could not wait, and that training should be entrusted to He Gang, a clerk in the Ministry of War. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 太仆少卿馬紹愉奉使陛見，語及陳新甲主款事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Studs Ma Shaoyu, on an audience mission, spoke of Chen Xinjia's chief role in peace negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shaoyu, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Studs, had come to audience on a diplomatic mission and spoke of Chen Xinjia's leading role in the peace negotiations.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「如此，新甲當恤。」

translations.literal: The Prince said, "If so, Xinjia should receive posthumous favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "In that case Xinjia deserves imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 廷臣無應者，獨少詹事陳盟曰可。

translations.literal: No court minister responded; only Junior Mentor Chen Meng said it was acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: No one in court answered; only Junior Mentor Chen Meng said that would be fitting.

sentences.zh: 因命予恤，且追罪嘗劾新甲者。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered posthumous favor granted and moreover pursued punishment against those who had once impeached Xinjia.
translations.idiomatic: An order followed granting posthumous honors, and the court moved to punish those who had once impeached Xinjia.

sentences.zh: 廷臣懲劉孔昭殿上相爭事，不敢言。

translations.literal: Court ministers, chastened by Liu Kongzhao's courtroom brawl, dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers, still shaken by Liu Kongzhao's brawl in open court, dared not object.

sentences.zh: 子龍與同官李清交章力諫，事獲已。

translations.literal: Zilong and fellow officer Li Qing submitted successive memorials urging strongly against it; the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong and his colleague Li Qing filed memorial after memorial in fierce protest, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，列上防守要策，請召還故尚書鄭三俊，都御史易應昌、房可壯、孫晉，並可之。

translations.literal: Before long he submitted in succession key defensive measures and asked to recall former ministers Zheng Sanjun, censor-in-chiefs Yi Yingchang, Fang Kezhuang, and Sun Jin—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he laid out essential defensive measures and asked that former Minister Zheng Sanjun and Censor-in-Chiefs Yi Yingchang, Fang Kezhuang, and Sun Jin be recalled. All were approved.

sentences.zh: 又言：「中使四出搜巷。

translations.literal: He also said, "Imperial envoys went out on all sides searching the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported, "Palace envoys are fanning out through the lanes on search missions.

sentences.zh: 凡有女之家，黃紙貼額，持之而去，閭井騷然。

translations.literal: Wherever there was a household with daughters, yellow paper was pasted on the doorframe and they were taken away; neighborhoods were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At every house with daughters, yellow paper was pasted on the doorframe and the girls were carried off, throwing whole neighborhoods into panic.

sentences.zh: 明旨未經有司，中使私自搜采，甚非法紀。」

translations.literal: Clear edicts had not passed through regular officials; eunuch envoys searched and gathered on their own—this greatly violated law and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: No proper edict had come through the regular bureaucracy; the eunuch envoys were seizing people on their own authority, in gross violation of law.

sentences.zh: 乃命禁訛傳誑惑者。

translations.literal: He then ordered prohibition of rumor-mongering and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: An order was issued forbidding rumor-mongering and deception.

sentences.zh: 子龍又言：「中興之主，莫不身先士卒，故能光復舊物。

translations.literal: Zilong also said, "Restoration sovereigns have all led from the front, and so were able to recover what had been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong added, "Every sovereign who restored a fallen dynasty led from the front, and that is how the old realm was recovered.

sentences.zh: 今入國門再旬矣，人情泄沓，無異升平。

translations.literal: Now it has been two ten-day periods since entering the capital gate, yet public sentiment is lax, no different from peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we have been inside the capital gates for twenty days already, and the mood is slack, as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 清歌漏舟之中，痛飲焚屋之內，臣不知其所終。

translations.literal: Clear songs in a leaking boat, deep drinking inside a burning house—I do not know where this will end.
translations.idiomatic: We sing softly in a boat already leaking, and drink deep in a house already burning. I cannot see where this ends.

sentences.zh: 其始皆起於姑息一二武臣，以至凡百政令皆因循遵養，臣甚為之寒心也。」

translations.literal: It all began with indulgence of one or two military men, until every sort of policy merely followed and preserved the status quo; the minister is deeply alarmed by this.
translations.idiomatic: It began with indulgence toward one or two generals, and now every measure merely drifts along in complacency. Your servant is deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 亦不聽。

translations.literal: This too went unheard.
translations.idiomatic: This too went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 明年二月乞終養去。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year he requested leave to complete mourning and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he asked to be released for full mourning and left office.

sentences.zh: 子龍與同邑夏允彜皆負重名，允彜死，子龍念祖母年九十，不忍割，遁為僧。

translations.literal: Zilong and fellow-townsman Xia Yunyi both bore great fame; when Yunyi died, Zilong thought of his grandmother at ninety and could not bear to leave her; he fled and became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong and his fellow townsman Xia Yunyi both enjoyed great renown. After Yunyi's death, Zilong thought of his grandmother, then ninety, and could not bring himself to abandon her; he went into hiding and became a monk.

sentences.zh: 尋以受魯王部院職銜，結太湖兵，欲舉事。

translations.literal: Before long, having accepted a ministry and court title from the Prince of Lu, he gathered troops at Lake Tai, intending to raise an uprising.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, having accepted a ministry and court commission from the Prince of Lu, he gathered forces on Lake Tai, intending to rise in arms.

sentences.zh: 事露被獲，乘間投水死。

translations.literal: When the plot was exposed he was captured; seizing an opening he drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered he was seized; finding an opening, he threw himself into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 夏允彜，字彜仲。

translations.literal: Xia Yunyi, styled Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yunyi, courtesy name Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉於鄉，好古博學，工屬文。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he passed the provincial examinations; fond of antiquity and wide learning, skilled at parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: In early manhood he passed the provincial examinations. He loved antiquity, read widely, and wrote accomplished prose.

sentences.zh: 是時東林講席盛，蘇州高才生張溥、楊廷樞等慕之，結文會名復社。

translations.literal: At that time Donglin lecture halls flourished; talented youths of Suzhou, Zhang Pu and Yang Tinghu and others, admired them and formed a literary society named Fushe.
translations.idiomatic: Donglin lecture halls were then at their height. Talented young men of Suzhou—Zhang Pu, Yang Tinghu, and others—looked to them and formed a literary society called Fushe, the Restoration Society.

sentences.zh: 允彜與同邑陳子龍、徐孚遠、王光承等亦結幾社相應和。

translations.literal: Yunyi with fellow-townsman Chen Zilong, Xu Fuyuan, Wang Guangcheng, and others also formed the Jishe society in mutual response.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi, together with Chen Zilong, Xu Fuyuan, Wang Guangcheng, and other townsmen, formed the Jishe society in answer.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年，與子龍同成進士，授長樂知縣，善決疑獄。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he and Zilong both received their jinshi degrees; he was appointed magistrate of Changle and excelled at resolving doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he and Zilong both received their jinshi degrees. He was appointed magistrate of Changle and had a gift for resolving hard cases.

sentences.zh: 他郡邑不能決者，上官多下長樂。

translations.literal: Cases other prefectures and counties could not decide were mostly referred to Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Cases that other prefectures and counties could not settle were often sent down to Changle.

sentences.zh: 居五年，邑大治。

translations.literal: After five years in office the district was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in office the district was thoroughly well governed.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書鄭三俊舉天下廉能知縣七人，以允彜為首。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zheng Sanjun nominated seven incorrupt and able magistrates under Heaven, with Yunyi first.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zheng Sanjun nominated the seven most incorrupt and capable magistrates in the realm, with Yunyi at the head of the list.

sentences.zh: 帝召見，大臣方嶽貢等力稱其賢，將特擢。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him for audience; minister Fang Yuegong and others strongly praised his worth; a special promotion was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him to audience. Minister Fang Yuegong and others spoke forcefully of his merit, and a special promotion was in the offing.

sentences.zh: 會丁母憂，未及用。

translations.literal: Just then he entered mourning for his mother and the appointment was not made in time.
translations.idiomatic: Just then he entered mourning for his mother, and the appointment never came.

sentences.zh: 北都變聞，允彜走謁尚書史可法，與謀興復。

translations.literal: When word came of the northern capital's fall, Yunyi went to visit Minister Shi Kefa and plotted restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When news came of the fall of the northern capital, Yunyi went to see Minister Shi Kefa and joined in plans for restoration.

sentences.zh: 聞福王立，乃還。

translations.literal: Hearing the Prince of Fu had been enthroned, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Prince of Fu had been enthroned, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 其年五月擢吏部考功司主事。

translations.literal: That fifth month he was promoted to chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: That fifth month he was promoted to chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 疏請終制，不赴。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to complete mourning and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to complete his mourning period and did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 御史徐復陽希要人旨，劾允彜及其同官文德翼居喪授職為非制，以兩人皆東林也。

translations.literal: Censor Xu Fuyang, hoping to please powerful men's intent, impeached Yunyi and fellow officer Wen Deyi for receiving office while in mourning as against regulations, because both were Donglin men.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Fuyang, currying favor with the powerful, impeached Yunyi and his colleague Wen Deyi for accepting office while still in mourning, a breach of regulation—because both were Donglin men.

sentences.zh: 兩人實未嘗赴官，無可罪。

translations.literal: The two in fact had never taken office—there was nothing with which to charge them.
translations.idiomatic: In fact neither man had ever taken up his post; there was no real offense.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張捷遽議貶秩調用。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhang Jie hastily proposed demotion in rank and reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhang Jie hastily proposed demoting them in rank and reassigning them elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 未幾，南都失，仿徨山澤間，欲有所為。

translations.literal: Before long the southern capital fell; he wandered among mountains and marshes, wishing to accomplish something.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the southern capital fell. He wandered among mountains and marshes, still hoping to act.

sentences.zh: 聞友人侯峒曾、黃淳耀、徐氵幵等皆死，乃以八月中賦絕命詞，自投深淵以死。

translations.literal: Learning that friends Hou Tongzeng, Huang Chunyao, Xu Kai, and others had all died, in the eighth month he composed a death verse and threw himself into deep waters to die.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that his friends Hou Tongzeng, Huang Chunyao, Xu Kai, and others had all died, he wrote a final poem in the eighth month and cast himself into deep waters.

sentences.zh: 允彜死後二年，子完淳、兄之旭並以陳子龍獄詞連及，亦死。

translations.literal: Two years after Yunyi's death, his son Wanchun and elder brother Zhixu were both implicated through Chen Zilong's court testimony and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after Yunyi's death, his son Wanchun and elder brother Zhixu were both implicated in Chen Zilong's trial testimony and were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 而同社徐孚遠，舉於鄉，因松江破，遁入海，死於島中。

translations.literal: Fellow society member Xu Fuyuan, successful at the provincial examinations, when Songjiang fell fled to sea and died on an island.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fuyuan, another member of the society and a provincial graduate, fled to sea when Songjiang fell and died on an island.

sentences.zh: 侯峒曾，字豫瞻，嘉定縣人。

translations.literal: Hou Tongzeng, styled Yuzhan, was a man of Jiading County.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tongzeng, courtesy name Yuzhan, was a native of Jiading County.

sentences.zh: 給事中震旸子也。

translations.literal: He was the son of supervising secretary Zhenyong.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of supervising secretary Zhenyong.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年成進士，授南京武選司主事，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi; appointed chief clerk of the Nanjing Bureau of Military Selection; he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of Tianqi and was appointed chief clerk of the Nanjing Bureau of Military Selection, then entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年入都。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張鳳翼薦為職方郎中，峒曾力辭，乃改南京文選司主事。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Fengyi recommended him for director of the Bureau of Appointments; Tongzeng strongly declined, and he was changed to chief clerk of the Nanjing Bureau of Civil Selection.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Fengyi recommended him for director of the Bureau of Appointments, but Tongzeng firmly declined and was instead made chief clerk of the Nanjing Bureau of Civil Selection.

sentences.zh: 由稽勛郎中遷江西提學參議。

translations.literal: From director in the Bureau of Honors he was transferred to educational commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from director in the Bureau of Honors, he was transferred to educational commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 給事中耿始然督賦至，他監司以屬禮見，峒曾獨與抗禮。

translations.literal: When supervising secretary Geng Shiran arrived on a tax-supervision tour, other commissioners received him with ceremonial precedence; Tongzeng alone met him as an equal.
translations.idiomatic: When supervising secretary Geng Shiran arrived on a tax-inspection tour, the other commissioners received him with subordinate ceremony; Tongzeng alone treated him as an equal.

sentences.zh: 益王勢方熾，歲試黜兩宗生，王怒，使人誚讓，峒曾不為動。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi was then at the height of power; in the annual examination he failed two clansmen of the princely house; the prince was angry and sent someone to reprove him, but Tongzeng was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi was then at the height of his influence. At the annual examination Tongzeng failed two members of the princely clan; the prince was furious and sent men to rebuke him, but Tongzeng would not budge.

sentences.zh: 遷廣東副使，不赴。

translations.literal: Transferred to vice commissioner of Guangdong; he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Guangdong but did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 起浙江右參政，分守嘉、湖。

translations.literal: Recalled as right vice commissioner of Zhejiang, with divided duty guarding Jia and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, with divided duty guarding Jiaxing and Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 漕卒擊傷秀水知縣李向中，峒曾請於撫按，捕戮首惡，部內肅然。

translations.literal: Transport grain soldiers wounded Xiushui magistrate Li Xiangzhong; Tongzeng requested of the grand coordinator and censor that the ringleader be arrested and executed; the region was then orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-transport soldiers wounded Xiushui magistrate Li Xiangzhong. Tongzeng petitioned the grand coordinator and censor to arrest and execute the ringleader, and order was restored throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書鄭三俊舉天下賢能監司五人，峒曾與焉。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zheng Sanjun nominated five worthy and able commissioners under Heaven; Tongzeng was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zheng Sanjun nominated the five most worthy and capable commissioners in the realm, and Tongzeng was among them.

sentences.zh: 召為順天府丞，未赴而京師陷。

translations.literal: Summoned as vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture; before he arrived the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture, but before he could take up the post the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王時，用為左通政，辭不就。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was used as left vice minister of communications; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was appointed Left Vice Minister of Communications, but he declined and would not serve.

sentences.zh: 及南京覆，州縣多起兵自保。

translations.literal: When Nanjing fell, prefectures and counties everywhere rose in arms to protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing fell, one prefecture and county after another took up arms to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 嘉定士民推峒曾為倡，偕裏人黃淳耀、張錫眉、董用圓、馬元調、唐全昌、夏雲蛟等誓死固守。

translations.literal: The gentry and commoners of Jiading chose Dongceng as their leader; together with fellow townspeople Huang Chunyao, Zhang Ximei, Dong Yongyuan, Ma Yuantiao, Tang Quanchang, Xia Yunjiao, and others they vowed to die rather than yield and held the city fast.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and people of Jiading put Hou Dongceng at their head. With Huang Chunyao, Zhang Ximei, Dong Yongyuan, Ma Yuantiao, Tang Quanchang, Xia Yunjiao, and other local men, they swore to hold the city unto death.

sentences.zh: 大清兵來攻，峒曾乞師於吳淞總兵官吳誌葵。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops came to attack; Dongceng begged troops from Wusong regional commander Wu Zhikui.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing armies moved against the city. Dongceng pleaded for reinforcements from Wu Zhikui, the regional commander at Wusong.

sentences.zh: 誌葵遣遊擊蔡祥以七百人來赴，一戰失利，束甲遁，外援遂絕，城中矢石俱盡。

translations.literal: Zhikui sent raiding commander Cai Xiang with seven hundred men to their aid; after one battle they were defeated, gathered their armor and fled; outside aid was thus cut off, and arrows and stones within the city were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhikui dispatched the raiding commander Cai Xiang with seven hundred men. One clash went badly; they strapped on their armor and fled. Outside help was gone, and the city had spent its last arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 七月三日大雨，城隅崩，架巨木支之。

translations.literal: On the third day of the seventh month heavy rain fell; a corner of the wall collapsed, and they erected huge timbers to prop it up.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the seventh month a downpour brought down a section of wall; the defenders raised great beams to shore it up.

sentences.zh: 明日雨益甚，城大崩，大清兵入。

translations.literal: The next day the rain grew worse; the wall collapsed on a large scale, and Our Great Qing troops entered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rain intensified and the wall gave way in a great breach. Our Great Qing troops poured in.

sentences.zh: 峒曾拜家廟，挈二子元演、元潔並沈於池。

translations.literal: Dongceng bowed at the family temple, took his two sons Yuanyan and Yuanjie, and together they drowned themselves in a pool.
translations.idiomatic: Dongceng paid his respects at the family shrine, then took his sons Yuanyan and Yuanjie and drowned with them in a pool.

sentences.zh: 錫眉、用圓、元調、全昌、雲蛟皆死之。

translations.literal: Ximei, Yongyuan, Yuantiao, Quanchang, and Yunjiao all died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ximei, Dong Yongyuan, Ma Yuantiao, Tang Quanchang, and Xia Yunjiao all died defending the city.

sentences.zh: 錫眉、用圓皆舉人。

translations.literal: Ximei and Yongyuan were both juren.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ximei and Dong Yongyuan had both passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 用圓官秀水教諭。

translations.literal: Yongyuan held office as instructor at Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yongyuan had served as instructor in Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 元調、全昌、雲蛟並諸生。

translations.literal: Yuantiao, Quanchang, and Yunjiao were all licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuantiao, Tang Quanchang, and Xia Yunjiao were all licentiates.

sentences.zh: 其時聚眾城守而死者有江陰閻應元、昆山朱集璜之屬。

translations.literal: At that time among those who gathered crowds to defend cities and died were Yan Chengyuan of Jiangyin, Zhu Jihuang of Kunshan, and their like.
translations.idiomatic: Others who rallied townsfolk to hold their cities and died in the attempt included Yan Chengyuan at Jiangyin and Zhu Jihuang at Kunshan, among others.

sentences.zh: 應元，字麗亨，順天通州人。

translations.literal: Chengyuan, style name Liheng, was a native of Tongzhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chengyuan, styled Liheng, came from Tongzhou in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，為江陰典史。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he served as registrar of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he was registrar of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 十七年，海賊顧三麻人黃田港，應元往禦，手射殺三人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year sea bandits under Gu San entered Huangtian Harbor; Chengyuan went to repel them and with his own hand shot and killed three men.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the pirate Gu San entered Huangtian Harbor. Chengyuan went to meet him and killed three men with his own bow.

sentences.zh: 賊退，以功遷英德主簿，道阻不赴，寓居江陰。

translations.literal: The bandits retreated; for his merit he was promoted to chief clerk of Yingde, but the roads were blocked and he did not take up the post, residing instead in Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates withdrew he was promoted to chief clerk of Yingde for his service, but blocked roads kept him from taking up the post and he settled in Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，南京亡，列城皆下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year Nanjing fell, and city after city submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the fifth month, Nanjing fell and one walled town after another surrendered.

sentences.zh: 閏六月朔，諸生許用倡言守城，遠近應者數萬人。

translations.literal: On the first day of the intercalary sixth month, student Xu Yong proposed holding the city; tens of thousands from near and far responded.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the intercalary sixth month the licentiate Xu Yong called for the city to be held, and tens of thousands from near and far answered.

sentences.zh: 典史陳明遇主兵，用徽人邵康公為將。

translations.literal: Registrar Chen Mingyu took charge of the troops, and Yong appointed Shao Kangong, a man of Huizhou, as general.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Chen Mingyu commanded the troops; Xu Yong made Shao Kangong of Huizhou their general.

sentences.zh: 而前都司周瑞龍泊江口，相掎角。

translations.literal: Meanwhile former company commander Zhou Ruilong anchored at the river mouth, forming a pincer with them.
translations.idiomatic: Former company commander Zhou Ruilong lay at anchor in the river mouth, coordinating with them in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 戰失利，大清兵逼城下。

translations.literal: They were defeated in battle, and Our Great Qing troops pressed up to the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders lost the fight, and Our Great Qing forces closed on the walls.

sentences.zh: 徽人程璧盡散家貲充餉，而身乞師於吳淞總兵官吳誌葵。

translations.literal: Cheng Bi, a man of Huizhou, spent his entire family fortune to pay the troops, while he himself went to beg reinforcements from Wusong regional commander Wu Zhikui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Bi of Huizhou poured out his whole fortune to feed the army, then went in person to beg troops from Wu Zhikui at Wusong.

sentences.zh: 誌葵至，璧遂不返。

translations.literal: When Zhikui arrived, Bi then did not return.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhikui came, Bi never returned.

sentences.zh: 康公戰不勝，瑞龍水軍亦敗去，明遇乃請應元入城，屬以兵事。

translations.literal: Kangong could not win the fight; Ruilong's naval force was also defeated and withdrew; Mingyu then invited Chengyuan into the city and entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kangong could not prevail; Ruilong's fleet was beaten and withdrew. Mingyu then brought Chengyuan into the city and put the defense in his hands.

sentences.zh: 大清兵力攻城，應元守甚固。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops exerted their strength to attack the city; Chengyuan defended it very firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing armies threw their full weight against the city, but Chengyuan's defense held firm.

sentences.zh: 東平伯劉良佐用牛皮帳攻城東北，城中用炮石力擊。

translations.literal: Earl of Dongping Liu Liangzuo used ox-hide shields to attack the northeast; the city used cannon and stones to strike back with full force.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Dongping, Liu Liangzuo, assaulted the northeast with ox-hide mantlets while the defenders answered with cannon and stones.

sentences.zh: 良佐乃移營十方庵，令僧陳利害。

translations.literal: Liangzuo then moved camp to Shifang Temple and sent a monk to explain the advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo shifted his camp to Shifang Temple and sent a monk to lay out the costs and consequences.

sentences.zh: 良佐旋策馬至，應元誓以大義，屹不動。

translations.literal: Liangzuo shortly rode up in person; Chengyuan swore by the higher cause and stood unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo soon rode up himself. Chengyuan answered with an oath to the greater cause and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 及松江破，大清兵來益眾，四圍發大炮，城中死傷無算，猶固守。

translations.literal: When Songjiang fell, Our Great Qing troops came in ever greater numbers; they set up great cannon on all four sides; dead and wounded within the city were beyond counting, yet they still held firm.
translations.idiomatic: After Songjiang fell, Our Great Qing forces grew ever more numerous. Great guns ringed the city on every side; casualties within the walls were beyond count, yet the defenders still held.

sentences.zh: 八月二十一日，大清兵從祥符寺後城入，眾猶巷戰，男婦投池井皆滿。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eighth month Our Great Qing troops entered through the wall behind Xiangfu Temple; the people still fought in the lanes; men and women who threw themselves into pools and wells filled them completely.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the eighth month Our Great Qing troops broke in through the wall behind Xiangfu Temple. Fighting continued in the lanes; men and women drowned themselves in pools and wells until they were full.

sentences.zh: 明遇、用皆舉家自焚。

translations.literal: Mingyu and Yong both burned their entire families with themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyu and Xu Yong each burned their whole households with themselves.

sentences.zh: 應元赴水，被曳出，死之。

translations.literal: Chengyuan went into the water but was dragged out and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan threw himself into the water, was pulled out, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 訓導馮厚敦冠帶縊於明倫堂，娣及妻王結礻任投井死。

translations.literal: Instructor Feng Houdun put on his cap and belt and hanged himself in the Hall of Bright Ethics; his sister-in-law and his wife Wang linked sleeves and threw themselves into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Feng Houdun, cap and belt in place, hanged himself in the Hall of Bright Ethics. His sister-in-law and his wife Wang linked sleeves and cast themselves into a well.

sentences.zh: 裏居中書舍人戚勛令妻及子女、子婦先縊，乃舉火自焚，從死者二十人。

translations.literal: Qi Xun, a Central Secretariat secretary residing in the neighborhood, had his wife, children, and daughters-in-law hang themselves first, then set fire and burned himself; twenty people died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xun, a Central Secretariat secretary of the neighborhood, had his wife, children, and daughters-in-law hang themselves first, then set himself ablaze. Twenty died with him.

sentences.zh: 舉人夏維新，諸生王華、呂九韶自刎死。

translations.literal: Juren Xia Weixin and students Wang Hua and Lü Jiushao cut their own throats and died.
translations.idiomatic: The juren Xia Weixin and the licentiates Wang Hua and Lü Jiushao slit their own throats.

sentences.zh: 貢生黃毓祺者，好學，有盛名，精釋氏學。

translations.literal: There was a tribute student Huang Yuqi, fond of learning, of great renown, accomplished in Buddhist studies.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yuqi, a tribute student, loved learning, enjoyed wide fame, and was deeply versed in Buddhist doctrine.

sentences.zh: 與門人徐趨舉兵行塘，以應城內兵。

translations.literal: With his disciple Xu Qu he raised troops at Xingtang to coordinate with the forces inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: With his disciple Xu Qu he raised troops at Xingtang to support the defenders within the walls.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，兩人逸去。

translations.literal: When the city fell, both men escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, both escaped.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，趨偵江陰無備，率壯士十四人襲之。

translations.literal: The next winter Qu scouted and found Jiangyin unguarded; he led fourteen stalwart men in an attack.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter Xu Qu found Jiangyin undefended and led fourteen stalwart men in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 不克，皆死。

translations.literal: They did not succeed; all died.
translations.idiomatic: They failed, and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 毓祺既逸去，避江北。

translations.literal: Yuqi having escaped took refuge north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yuqi, having escaped, took refuge north of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 其子大湛、大洪被收，兄弟方爭死。

translations.literal: His sons Dazhan and Dahong were arrested; the brothers were each vying to die in the other's place.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Dazhan and Dahong were seized; each brother tried to claim death for himself.

sentences.zh: 而毓祺以敕印事發，逮系江寧獄，將刑，其門人告之期，命取襲衣自斂，趺坐而逝。

translations.literal: But Yuqi was implicated in a matter concerning an imperial seal; he was arrested and imprisoned in Jiangning; as execution approached his disciple informed him of the date; he ordered his funeral garments brought, composed himself in seated meditation, and passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqi was then implicated in a case involving an imperial seal, seized, and held in the Jiangning jail. As the day of execution drew near a disciple told him when it would come. He had his burial clothes brought, sat cross-legged, and died.

sentences.zh: 朱集璜，字以發，昆山貢生。

translations.literal: Zhu Jihuang, style name Yifa, was a tribute student of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jihuang, styled Yifa, was a tribute student of Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 學行為鄉里所推，教授弟子數百人。

translations.literal: His learning and conduct were esteemed by his neighborhood; he instructed several hundred disciples.
translations.idiomatic: His learning and conduct won the respect of his community, and he taught several hundred disciples.

sentences.zh: 南京既亡，昆山議拒守，而縣丞閻茂才已遣使迎降。

translations.literal: Nanjing having fallen, Kunshan debated refusing to submit and defending the city, but assistant magistrate Yan Maocai had already sent envoys to welcome surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing fell, Kunshan debated holding out, but Assistant Magistrate Yan Maocai had already sent envoys to welcome the conquerors.

sentences.zh: 縣人共執殺茂才，以六月望，推舊將王佐才為帥，集璜及周室瑜、陶琰、陳大任等共舉兵。

translations.literal: The county people together seized and killed Maocai; on the fifteenth of the sixth month they chose former general Wang Zuocai as commander; Jihuang together with Zhou Shiyu, Tao Yan, Chen Daren, and others jointly raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: The county people seized and killed Maocai. On the fifteenth of the sixth month they chose the old general Wang Zuocai as commander; Jihuang, Zhou Shiyu, Tao Yan, Chen Daren, and others raised arms together.

sentences.zh: 參將陳宏勛、前知縣楊永言率壯士百人為助。

translations.literal: Brigade commander Chen Hongxun and former magistrate Yang Yongyan led a hundred stalwart men to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Commander Chen Hongxun and former Magistrate Yang Yongyan brought a hundred stalwart men to their aid.

sentences.zh: 佐才亦邑人，嘗官狼山副總兵，年老矣。

translations.literal: Zuocai was also a native of the county; he had once served as deputy regional commander at Langshan and was now old.
translations.idiomatic: Zuocai was a local man who had once served as deputy regional commander at Langshan and was by then advanced in years.

sentences.zh: 大清兵至，宏勛率舟師迎戰，敗還，遊擊孫誌尹戰歿。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops arrived; Hongxun led the naval force to meet them in battle, was defeated and retreated; raiding commander Sun Zhiyin died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Our Great Qing forces arrived, Hongxun led the fleet out to fight, was beaten back, and the raiding commander Sun Zhiyin fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 城陷，永言遁去。

translations.literal: The city fell; Yongyan fled.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell, and Yongyan fled.

sentences.zh: 佐才縱民出走，而己冠帶坐帥府，被殺。

translations.literal: Zuocai let the people flee, but he himself, cap and belt in place, sat in the commander's hall and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuocai opened the gates for the people to escape, then sat in full cap and belt in the commander's hall and was killed.

sentences.zh: 集璜投東禪寺後河死。

translations.literal: Jihuang threw himself into the river behind Dongchan Temple and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jihuang drowned himself in the river behind Dongchan Temple.

sentences.zh: 門人孫道民、張謙同日死。

translations.literal: Disciples Sun Daomin and Zhang Qian died on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Sun Daomin and Zhang Qian died the same day.

sentences.zh: 室瑜、琰、大任亦死之。

translations.literal: Shiyu, Yan, and Daren also died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shiyu, Tao Yan, and Chen Daren died as well.

sentences.zh: 室瑜子朝礦、大任子思翰皆同死。

translations.literal: Shiyu's son Chaokuang and Daren's son Sihan both died with them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu's son Chaokuang and Daren's son Sihan died with them.

sentences.zh: 室瑜舉於鄉，官儀封知縣。

translations.literal: Shiyu passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shiyu had passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 琰、大任皆諸生。

translations.literal: Yan and Daren were both students.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Yan and Chen Daren were both licentiates.

sentences.zh: 時以守禦死者，蘇達道、莊萬程、陸世鏜、陸雲將、歸之甲、周復培、陸彥沖。

translations.literal: Those who died defending the city at that time included Su Dadao, Zhuang Wancheng, Lu Shiyao, Lu Yunjiang, Gui Zhijia, Zhou Fupei, and Lu Yanchong.
translations.idiomatic: Others who died in the defense included Su Dadao, Zhuang Wancheng, Lu Shiyao, Lu Yunjiang, Gui Zhijia, Zhou Fupei, and Lu Yanchong.

sentences.zh: 代父死者，沈征憲、朱國軾。

translations.literal: Those who died in their fathers' place were Shen Zhengxian and Zhu Guoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhengxian and Zhu Guoshi died in their fathers' stead.

sentences.zh: 救母死者，徐洺。

translations.literal: He who died saving his mother was Xu Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ming died saving his mother.

sentences.zh: 自盡者，徐溵、王在中、吳行貞。

translations.literal: Those who took their own lives were Xu Yin, Wang Zaizhong, and Wu Xingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Those who killed themselves included Xu Yin, Wang Zaizhong, and Wu Xingzhen.

sentences.zh: 楊文驄，字龍友，貴陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Wencong, style name Longyou, was a native of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wencong, styled Longyou, was a native of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 浙江參政師孔子。

translations.literal: He was the son of Yang Shikong, who had served as vice commissioner in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yang Shikong, who had held office as vice commissioner in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，官江寧知縣。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he served as magistrate of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he served as magistrate of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 御史詹兆恒劾其貪汙，奪官侯訊。

translations.literal: Censor Zhan Zhaoheng impeached him for corruption; his office was stripped and he awaited trial.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhan Zhaoheng impeached him for graft; he was dismissed and held for investigation.

sentences.zh: 事未竟，福王立於南京，文驄戚馬士英當國，起兵部主事，歷員外郎、郎中，皆監軍京口。

translations.literal: Before the case was concluded, the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing; Wencong's kinsman Ma Shiying held power; he was appointed chief clerk in the Ministry of War, then rose through vice director and director, all while supervising troops at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Before the case was settled, the Prince of Fu took the throne at Nanjing. Wencong's relative Ma Shiying dominated the court; Wencong was made chief clerk in the Ministry of War, then promoted through vice director and director, all the while supervising the army at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 以金山踞大江中，控制南北，請築城以資守禦，從之。

translations.literal: Because Jinshan stood in midstream on the great river and controlled north and south, he requested that a wall be built to aid defense, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jinshan rose from midstream in the Yangzi and commanded the crossing between north and south, he asked that walls be built there for defense, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 文驄善書，有文藻，好交遊，幹士英者多緣以進。

translations.literal: Wencong was skilled at calligraphy, had literary talent, and loved company; many who sought Shiying's favor advanced through him.
translations.idiomatic: Wencong wrote well, had literary gifts, and loved company; many who courted Ma Shiying's favor found their way through him.

sentences.zh: 其為人豪俠自喜，頗推獎名士，士亦以此附之。

translations.literal: By nature he was proud and generous, and he greatly promoted men of reputation; scholars in turn rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature bold and self-confident, generous in promoting men of note, and scholars gathered around him for that reason.

sentences.zh: 明年遷兵備副使，分巡常、鎮二府，監大將鄭鴻逵、鄭彩軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to vice commissioner for military affairs, touring Changzhou and Zhenjiang, and supervising the armies of the great generals Zheng Hongkui and Zheng Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became vice commissioner for military affairs with jurisdiction over Changzhou and Zhenjiang, overseeing the armies of the great generals Zheng Hongkui and Zheng Cai.

sentences.zh: 及大清兵臨江，文驄駐金山，扼大江而守。

translations.literal: When Our Great Qing troops reached the Yangzi, Wencong held Jinshan and blocked the great river in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Our Great Qing armies reached the Yangzi, Wencong held Jinshan and barred the river.

sentences.zh: 五月朔，擢右僉都御史，巡撫其地，兼督沿海諸軍。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of the region, with added charge over coastal forces.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of the region, with added command over coastal troops.

sentences.zh: 文驄乃還駐京口，合鴻逵等兵南岸，與大清兵隔江相持。

translations.literal: Wencong then returned to hold Jingkou, joining Hongkui's troops on the south bank to face Our Great Qing forces across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wencong then moved back to Jingkou, massing with Hongkui on the south bank to stand off Our Great Qing forces across the water.

sentences.zh: 大清兵編大筏，置燈火，夜放之中流，南岸軍發炮石，以為克敵也，日奏捷。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops lashed together great rafts, set lamps and fires on them, and at night floated them into midstream; the southern army fired cannon and stones, thinking they had beaten the enemy, and daily reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing forces bound great rafts, lit them with lamps and fire, and sent them drifting into midstream at night. The southern army answered with cannon and stones, took this for victory, and sent in daily reports of triumph.

sentences.zh: 初九日，大清兵乘霧潛濟，迫岸。

translations.literal: On the ninth day Our Great Qing troops crossed under cover of fog and pressed the shore.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth Our Great Qing troops crossed under cover of fog and closed on the bank.

sentences.zh: 諸軍始知，倉皇列陣甘露寺。

translations.literal: The armies only then realized it and in panic formed ranks at Ganlu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The southern troops realized too late and hurriedly formed battle lines at Ganlu Temple.

sentences.zh: 鐵騎沖之，悉潰。

translations.literal: Iron cavalry charged them and they all broke.
translations.idiomatic: Iron cavalry smashed into them, and the whole line collapsed.

sentences.zh: 文驄走蘇州。

translations.literal: Wencong fled to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wencong fled to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三日，大清兵破南京，百官盡降。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day Our Great Qing troops took Nanjing, and officials one and all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth Our Great Qing forces broke Nanjing, and the officials all submitted.

sentences.zh: 命鴻臚丞黃家鼒往蘇州安撫，文驄襲殺之，遂走處州。

translations.literal: An order was issued for Honglu Court director Huang Jiazi to go to Suzhou to reassure the people; Wencong ambushed and killed him, then fled to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Huang Jiazi of the Honglu Court to Suzhou to pacify the region. Wencong waylaid and killed him, then fled to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時唐王已自立於福州矣。

translations.literal: By then the Tang Prince had already declared himself at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Tang Prince had already proclaimed himself at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，唐王在鎮江時，與文驄交好。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Tang Prince was at Zhenjiang, he and Wencong had been on friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the Tang Prince was at Zhenjiang, he and Wencong had been close.

sentences.zh: 至是，文驄遣使奉表稱賀。

translations.literal: At this point Wencong sent an envoy with a memorial of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Wencong now sent an envoy with a memorial of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 鴻逵又數薦，乃拜兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，提督軍務，令圖南京。

translations.literal: Hongkui repeatedly recommended him, and he was appointed right vice minister of War and concurrent right vice censor-in-chief, with charge of military affairs and orders to plan the recovery of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongkui recommended him again and again, and he was made right vice minister of War and concurrent right vice censor-in-chief with charge of military affairs, charged with planning the recovery of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 加其子鼎卿左都督、太子太保。

translations.literal: His son Dingqing was made Left Chief Commandant and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dingqing was made Left Chief Commandant and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 鼎卿，士英甥也。

translations.literal: Dingqing was Shiying's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Dingqing was Ma Shiying's nephew.

sentences.zh: 士英遣迎福王，遇王於淮安。

translations.literal: Shiying was sent to welcome the Prince of Fu and met the prince at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying had been sent to welcome the Prince of Fu and met him at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 王貧寠甚，鼎卿赒給之，王與定布衣交，以故寵鼎卿甚。

translations.literal: The prince was very poor and destitute; Dingqing gave him relief; the prince made a pact of friendship in plain cloth with him, and for that reason favored Dingqing greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was desperately poor. Dingqing gave him aid, and the prince bound himself to him in a pact of plain-cloth friendship; for that reason he favored Dingqing deeply.

sentences.zh: 及鼎卿上謁，王以故人子遇之，獎其父子，擬以漢朝大、小耿。

translations.literal: When Dingqing came to audience, the prince received him as the son of an old friend, praised father and son, and likened them to the Elder and Younger Geng of the Han dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingqing presented himself at court, the prince received him as the son of an old friend, praised both father and son, and compared them to the Elder and Younger Geng of Han.

sentences.zh: 然其父子以士英故，多為人詆諆。

translations.literal: Yet because of Shiying, father and son were much slandered by others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of Ma Shiying, father and son were widely reviled.

sentences.zh: 明年，衢州告急。

translations.literal: The next year Quzhou reported urgent danger.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Quzhou sent word that it was in peril.

sentences.zh: 誠意侯劉孔昭亦駐處州，王令文驄與共援衢。

translations.literal: Marquis of Chengyi Liu Kongzhao was also stationed at Chuzhou; the prince ordered Wencong to join him in relieving Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Chengyi, Liu Kongzhao, was also at Chuzhou; the prince ordered Wencong to join him in relieving Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 七月，大清兵至，文驄不能禦，退至浦城，為追騎所獲，與監紀孫臨俱不降被戮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Our Great Qing troops arrived; Wencong could not hold them off, retreated to Pucheng, was overtaken by pursuing cavalry, and together with supervisory aide Sun Lin refused to submit and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Our Great Qing forces arrived. Wencong could not hold them, fell back to Pucheng, was caught by pursuing horsemen, and he and the supervisory aide Sun Lin were executed for refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 臨，字武公，桐城人，兵部侍郎晉之弟。

translations.literal: Lin, style name Wugong, was a native of Tongcheng and younger brother of Vice Minister of War Jin Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin, styled Wugong, came from Tongcheng and was the younger brother of Vice Minister of War Jin Zhi.

sentences.zh: 文驄招入幕，奏為職方主事，竟與同死。

translations.literal: Wencong recruited him into his staff, memorialized for him as director in the Bureau of Appointments, and in the end he died together with Wencong.
translations.idiomatic: Wencong brought him into his staff, had him appointed director in the Bureau of Appointments, and in the end he died with Wencong.

sentences.zh: 其時起兵旁掠郡縣者有吳易，字日生，吳江人。

translations.literal: At that time among those who raised troops and raided neighboring prefectures and counties was Wu Yi, style name Risheng, a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time one who raised troops and raided neighboring prefectures and counties was Wu Yi of Wujiang, styled Risheng.

sentences.zh: 生有膂力，跅弛不羈。

translations.literal: From birth he had great physical strength and was wild and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He was born with great strength and lived in wild, unrestrained fashion.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，成進士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chongzhen reign he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 福王時，謁史可法於揚州。

translations.literal: During the time of the Prince of Fu, he paid a visit to Shi Kefa at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, he called on Shi Kefa at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 可法異其才，題授職方主事，為己監軍。

translations.literal: Kefa was struck by his talent, recommended him for appointment as a director in the Bureau of Appointments, and made him his supervising officer.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa was impressed by his ability, recommended him for appointment as a director in the Bureau of Appointments, and took him on as his supervising officer.

sentences.zh: 明年，奉檄征餉江南，未還而揚州失，已而吳江亦失。

translations.literal: The next year, bearing an edict to collect provisions in Jiangnan, he had not yet returned when Yangzhou fell, and soon afterward Wujiang fell as well.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, dispatched under edict to levy provisions in Jiangnan, he had not yet returned when Yangzhou fell—and before long Wujiang fell too.

sentences.zh: 易走太湖，與同邑舉人孫兆奎，諸生沈自駉、自炳，武進吳福之等謀舉兵。

translations.literal: Yi fled to Lake Tai, and together with fellow-townsmen the juren Sun Zhaokui, the students Shen Zijing and Zibing, and Wu Fuzhi of Wujin, among others, plotted to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yi fled to Lake Tai and, with his fellow townsman the juren Sun Zhaokui, the students Shen Zijing and Zibing, Wu Fuzhi of Wujin, and others, plotted to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 旬日得千余人，屯於長白蕩，出沒旁近諸縣，道路為梗。

translations.literal: Within ten days they rallied more than a thousand men, encamped at Changbai Lake, and ranged through the neighboring counties, blocking the roads.
translations.idiomatic: In ten days they mustered more than a thousand men, encamped at Changbai Lake, and raided the surrounding counties until the roads were impassable.

sentences.zh: 唐王聞之，授兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督江南諸軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang heard of it, he appointed him Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, with overall command of the armies of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Tang learned of this, he appointed Yi Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, putting him in overall command of the Jiangnan armies.

sentences.zh: 文驄奏易斬獲多，進為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Wencong memorialized that Yi's beheadings and captures were many, and he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wencong reported that Yi had taken many heads and prisoners in battle, and Yi was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 魯王亦授易兵部侍郎，封長興伯。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu also appointed Yi Vice Minister of War and enfeoffed him as Earl of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu likewise appointed Yi Vice Minister of War and enfeoffed him as Earl of Changxing.

sentences.zh: 八月，大清兵至，易遂敗走。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Our Great Qing troops arrived, and Yi was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Our Great Qing armies arrived; Yi was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 父承緒、妻沈及女皆投水死，自駉、自炳、福之亦死焉，兆奎被獲，一軍盡殲。

translations.literal: His father Chengxu, his wife Shen, and his daughter all drowned themselves; Zijing, Zibing, and Fuzhi also died there; Zhaokui was captured, and the whole army was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengxu, his wife Shen, and his daughter all drowned themselves. Zijing, Zibing, and Fuzhi died as well; Zhaokui was taken alive, and the entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 明年，易鄉人周瑞復聚眾長白蕩，迎易入其營。

translations.literal: The next year Yi's fellow townsman Zhou Rui again gathered a crowd at Changbai Lake and welcomed Yi into his camp.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yi's townsman Zhou Rui rallied men again at Changbai Lake and brought Yi into his camp.

sentences.zh: 八月，事泄被獲，死之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the affair leaked out; he was captured and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the plot was discovered; he was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 福之，鐘巒子也。

translations.literal: Fuzhi was the son of Zhong Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi was the son of Zhong Luan.

sentences.zh: 兆奎兵敗時，慮易妻女被辱，視其死而後行，故被獲。

translations.literal: When Zhaokui's army was defeated, fearing that Yi's wife and daughter would be dishonored, he saw to their deaths before departing, and so was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaokui's force was broken, he feared Yi's wife and daughter would be violated; he made sure they were dead before he left, and was therefore captured.

sentences.zh: 械至江寧，死之。

translations.literal: Shackled and brought to Jiangning, he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Bound in fetters and taken to Jiangning, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 陳潛夫，字元倩，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Chen Qianfu, styled Yuanqian, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qianfu, courtesy name Yuanqian, was a native of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 家貧落魄，好大言以駴俗。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he was down on his luck; he loved grand talk to startle the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor and adrift, he loved grand pronouncements that shocked conventional opinion.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年舉於鄉，益廣交遊，為豪舉，好臧否人，里中人惡之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examinations; he broadened his friendships still further, made extravagant gestures, and loved to praise or condemn others—people in the district hated him.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in the ninth year of Chongzhen, widened his circle of friends, made flamboyant gestures, and loved passing judgment on others; his neighbors despised him.

sentences.zh: 友人陸培兄弟為文逐潛夫，潛夫乃避居華亭。

translations.literal: His friend Lu Pei and his brothers wrote a piece of prose to drive Qianfu away, and Qianfu thereupon withdrew to live in Huating.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Lu Pei and Lu's brothers wrote an essay denouncing Qianfu, who thereupon withdrew and took refuge in Huating.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，授開封推官。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year he was appointed pushi of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixteenth year he was appointed investigating magistrate of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 大河南五郡盡為賊據，開封被河灌，城虛無人，長吏皆寄居封丘。

translations.literal: The five prefectures of southern Henan were entirely occupied by bandits; Kaifeng was flooded by the river, the city stood empty of people, and the chief officials all lodged at Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: All five prefectures of southern Henan had fallen to bandits. Kaifeng was inundated by the river, its walls stood empty, and the senior officials had all taken refuge at Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 有勸潛夫弗往者，不聽，馳之封丘。

translations.literal: Some urged Qianfu not to go; he would not listen, and galloped to Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Qianfu not to go; he refused to listen and rode at full speed to Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 會叛將陳永福率賊兵出山西，其子德為巡撫秦所式部將，縛巡按御史蘇京去。

translations.literal: Just then the rebel general Chen Yongfu led bandit troops out of Shanxi; his son De was a subordinate general of Grand Coordinator Qin Suoshi, and he bound Surveillance Commissioner Su Jing and carried him off.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment the turncoat general Chen Yongfu led rebel troops out of Shanxi. His son De served under Grand Coordinator Qin Suoshi as a subordinate commander; he seized Surveillance Commissioner Su Jing and absconded with him.

sentences.zh: 潛夫募民兵千，請於所式及總兵卜從善、許定國，令共剿，皆不肯行。

translations.literal: Qianfu recruited a thousand militiamen and requested Suoshi and the regional commanders Bu Congshan and Xu Dingguo to join in a joint suppression; none would go.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu raised a thousand militiamen and asked Suoshi and the regional commanders Bu Congshan and Xu Dingguo to join in a joint campaign of suppression; none would move.

sentences.zh: 潛夫乃以十七年正月奉周王渡河居杞縣，檄召旁近長吏，設高皇帝位，歃血誓固守。

translations.literal: Qianfu thereupon in the first month of the seventeenth year escorted the Prince of Zhou across the river to dwell at Qi County, issued summons to the neighboring chief officials, set up a seat for the High Emperor, and swore an oath of blood to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu then, in the first month of the seventeenth year, escorted the Prince of Zhou across the Yellow River to Qi County, summoned the neighboring magistrates, set up a seat for the dynastic founder, and swore a blood oath to stand fast.

sentences.zh: 賊所設偽巡撫梁啟隆居開封，他偽官散布郡邑間甚眾，而開封東西諸土寨剽掠公行，相攻殺無已。

translations.literal: The bandits' false grand coordinator Li Qilong dwelt at Kaifeng; their other false officials were scattered through the prefectures and counties in great numbers, while the fortified stockades east and west of Kaifeng plundered openly, attacking and killing one another without end.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' puppet grand coordinator Li Qilong held Kaifeng; their other false officials were scattered across the region in great numbers, while fortified stockades east and west of the city plundered openly and fought one another without cease.

sentences.zh: 潛夫轉側杞、陳留間，朝夕不自保。

translations.literal: Qianfu shifted back and forth between Qi and Chenliu; morning and evening he could not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu shuttled between Qi and Chenliu, never secure from one hour to the next.

sentences.zh: 聞西平寨副將劉洪起勇而好義，屢殺賊有功，躬往說之。

translations.literal: Hearing that the deputy general of Xiping Stockade, Liu Hongqi, was brave and public-spirited and had repeatedly killed bandits with merit, he went in person to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Liu Hongqi, deputy commander of Xiping Stockade, was bold and public-spirited and had repeatedly routed bandits with distinction, he went to persuade him in person.

sentences.zh: 五月五日方誓師，而都城失守。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month they were just about to muster the army when the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month they were just taking the field when word came that the capital had fallen.

sentences.zh: 報至，乃慟哭，令其下縞素。

translations.literal: When the report arrived, he wailed in grief and ordered his subordinates to wear unhemmed white mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the news arrived he broke into lamentation and ordered his men to don unhemmed white mourning.

sentences.zh: 洪起兵萬，號五萬，潛夫兵三千，俘杞偽官，啟隆聞風遁去。

translations.literal: Hongqi raised ten thousand troops and claimed fifty thousand; Qianfu had three thousand. They captured the false officials of Qi, and Qilong fled at the news.
translations.idiomatic: Hongqi mustered ten thousand men and claimed fifty thousand; Qianfu had three thousand. They seized the puppet officials at Qi, and Qilong fled at the first rumor.

sentences.zh: 遂渡河而北，大破賊將陳德於柳園。

translations.literal: They then crossed the river northward and routed the bandit general Chen De at Liuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They then crossed the river north and routed the rebel general Chen De at Liuyuan.

sentences.zh: 時李自成已敗走山西，而南陽賊乘間犯西平，洪起引還，潛夫亦隨而南。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng had already been defeated and fled to Shanxi, but bandits in Nanyang seized the opportunity to invade Xiping; Hongqi led his troops back, and Qianfu followed south as well.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Zicheng had already been beaten and driven back into Shanxi, but bandits in Nanyang seized the moment to strike at Xiping. Hongqi turned back, and Qianfu withdrew south with him.

sentences.zh: 福王立南京，潛夫傳露布至，朝中大喜，即擢監軍御史，巡按河南。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu established his court at Nanjing; when Qianfu's victory bulletin arrived, the court was greatly pleased and immediately promoted him to supervising censor with duty to tour and inspect Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu had established his court at Nanjing. When Qianfu's victory dispatch arrived, the court rejoiced and at once promoted him to supervising censor with authority to tour Henan.

sentences.zh: 潛夫乃入朝言：「中興在進取，王業不偏安。

translations.literal: Qianfu then entered court and said: "Restoration lies in advancing; a royal enterprise is not preserved by clinging to one corner.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu then appeared at court and said, "Restoration depends on taking the offensive; a royal enterprise is not saved by clinging to a corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南地，尺寸不可棄。

translations.literal: The lands of Shandong and Henan—not an inch may be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The territory of Shandong and Henan—not a single inch may be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 豪傑結寨自固者，引領待官軍。

translations.literal: Heroes who have fortified stockades and hold themselves firm stretch their necks awaiting the official armies.
translations.idiomatic: Local heroes who have fortified their camps and hold their ground are craning their necks, waiting for the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 誠分命藩鎮，以一軍出潁、壽，一軍出淮、徐，則眾心競奮，爭為我用。
