translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly divides command among the regional garrisons, with one army issuing from Ying and Shou and another from Huai and Xu, then every heart will compete in ardor and strive to serve us.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly divides command among the regional garrisons—one army out of Ying and Shou, another out of Huai and Xu—then every heart will burn to serve, each vying to be first.

sentences.zh: 更頒爵賞鼓舞，計遠近，畫城堡俾自守，而我督撫將帥屯銳師要害以策應之。

translations.literal: Issue ranks and rewards still further to inspire them; reckon distances near and far, assign walled strongholds for them to hold themselves, while our supervising officials and generals station crack troops at strategic points to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Issue still more ranks and rewards to stir them; measure distances near and far, assign walled strongholds for them to defend on their own, while our supervising officials and generals station elite troops at the key points to answer their calls.

sentences.zh: 寬則耕屯為食，急則披甲乘墉，一方有警，前後救援，長河不足守也。

translations.literal: In quiet times let them farm and garrison for food; in urgency let them don armor and man the walls—when one quarter is alarmed, rescue comes before and behind; the long river alone is not enough to hold.
translations.idiomatic: In peace let them farm and garrison for their food; in crisis let them don armor and man the ramparts. When one sector is threatened, relief can come from front and rear—the long river alone cannot save us.

sentences.zh: 汴梁一路，臣聯絡素定，旬日可集十余萬人。

translations.literal: Along the Bianliang route my contacts are already fixed; within ten days more than a hundred thousand men can be gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Bianliang corridor my contacts are already in place; within ten days I can gather more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 誠稍給糗糧，容臣自將，臣當荷戈先驅，諸藩鎮為後勁，河南五郡可盡復。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will only supply rations in modest measure and allow me to lead in person, I shall take up spear and go in the van while the regional garrisons follow as the rear guard—the five prefectures of Henan can be wholly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will only furnish modest supplies and let me lead in person, I will take up my spear and go in the van while the regional garrisons follow as the rear guard—and the five Henan prefectures can be wholly recovered.

sentences.zh: 五郡既復，畫河為固，南連荊楚，西控秦關，北臨趙、衛，上之則恢復可望，下之則江淮永安，此今日至計也。

translations.literal: Once the five prefectures are recovered, mark out the river as a bulwark, link south to Jing and Chu, control westward the Qin Pass, and face north toward Zhao and Wei—then above, full restoration may be hoped for; below, the Jiang and Huai will be secure. This is the supreme plan for today.
translations.idiomatic: Once the five prefectures are recovered, make the river our bulwark—link south to Jing and Chu, hold west the Qin Pass, and face north toward Zhao and Wei. Then, at best, full restoration lies within reach; at least, the Jiang-Huai region will be secure. This is the supreme plan of the hour.

sentences.zh: 兩淮之上，何事多兵，督撫紛紜，並為虛設。

translations.literal: Above the Two Huai, why are there so many troops? Supervising officials are numerous and confused, all alike empty in function.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Two Huai, why are there so many troops? Supervising officials crowd one another in confusion, all of them hollow titles.

sentences.zh: 若不思外拒，專事退守，舉土地甲兵之眾致之他人，臣恐江淮亦未可保也。」

translations.literal: If we do not think of resisting outward but devote ourselves solely to retreat and defense, delivering the multitude of our lands, armor, and troops into others' hands, I fear the Jiang and Huai too may not be kept."
translations.idiomatic: If we refuse to resist outward and devote ourselves only to retreat and defense, handing over our lands, armor, and armies to others, I fear the Jiang-Huai region may not be kept either."

sentences.zh: 當是時，開封、汝寧間列寨百數，洪起最大；

translations.literal: At that time between Kaifeng and Runing there were several hundred stockades in a row; Hongqi was the largest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time several hundred stockades lined the route between Kaifeng and Runing; Hongqi's was the largest.

sentences.zh: 南陽列寨數十，蕭應訓最大，洛陽列寨亦數十，李際遇最大。

translations.literal: In Nanyang there were several dozen stockades; Xiao Yingxun was the largest. In Luoyang there were also several dozen; Li Jiyu was the largest.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanyang there were several dozen stockades, the largest under Xiao Yingxun. Around Luoyang there were several dozen as well, the largest under Li Jiyu.

sentences.zh: 諸帥中獨洪起欲效忠，潛夫請予掛印為將軍。

translations.literal: Among the commanders only Hongqi wished to show loyalty; Qianfu requested that he be granted an official seal and made a general.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the commanders, only Hongqi wished to serve in earnest; Qianfu asked that he be granted an official seal and appointed a general.

sentences.zh: 馬士英不聽，而用其姻婭越其傑巡撫河南。

translations.literal: Ma Shiying would not listen, but instead used his in-law Yue Qijie as grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying refused to listen and instead installed his in-law Yue Qijie as Grand Coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 潛夫自九月入覲，便道省親，甫五日即馳赴河上。

translations.literal: Qianfu had entered court for audience in the ninth month, stopped on the way to visit his parents, and after only five days galloped back to the river front.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu had entered court for audience in the ninth month, stopped briefly to visit his parents, and after only five days galloped back to the front on the river.

sentences.zh: 所建白皆不用，諸鎮兵無至者。

translations.literal: None of the proposals he had submitted was adopted, and no troops came from the various garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: None of his proposals was adopted, and no reinforcements came from the regional garrisons.

sentences.zh: 其傑老憊不知兵。

translations.literal: Qijie was old, worn out, and ignorant of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qijie was elderly, exhausted, and knew nothing of war.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張縉彥總督河南、山東軍務，止提空名，不能馭諸將。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Jinyan had overall command of military affairs in Henan and Shandong, but bore only an empty title and could not control the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Jinyan held nominal overall command of Henan and Shandong, but his title was empty and he could not command the generals.

sentences.zh: 其冬，應訓復南陽及泌陽、舞陽、桐柏，遣子三傑獻捷。

translations.literal: That winter Yingxun recovered Nanyang together with Biyang, Wuyang, and Tongbai, and sent his son Sanjie to present the victory report.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yingxun recovered Nanyang along with Biyang, Wuyang, and Tongbai, and sent his son Sanjie to report the victory.

sentences.zh: 潛夫授告身，飲之灑，鼓吹旌旗前導出。

translations.literal: Qianfu granted him a commission, gave him wine to drink, and saw him out with drums, horns, and banners leading the way.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu issued him a commission, treated him to wine, and sent him off with drums, horns, and banners leading the way.

sentences.zh: 三傑喜過望，往謁其傑。

translations.literal: Sanjie was delighted beyond expectation and went to pay his respects to Qijie.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjie was overjoyed beyond all expectation and went to pay his respects to Qijie.

sentences.zh: 其傑故為尊嚴，厲辭詰責，詆為賊。

translations.literal: Qijie deliberately put on an air of dignity, spoke harshly in rebuke, and denounced him as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Qijie deliberately assumed an air of majesty, rebuked him in harsh words, and denounced him as a bandit.

sentences.zh: 三傑泣而出，萌異心。

translations.literal: Sanjie wept as he went out, and a rebellious heart was born.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjie left in tears, already turning disloyal in his heart.

sentences.zh: 潛夫過諸寨，皆鐃吹送迎；

translations.literal: When Qianfu passed through the various stockades, all sent out drums and horns to welcome and escort him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianfu passed through the stockades, each sent out drums and horns to welcome and escort him.

sentences.zh: 其傑間過之，諸寨皆閉門不出。

translations.literal: When Qijie happened to pass by, every stockade shut its gates and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Qijie happened to pass through, every stockade shut its gates and refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 其傑恚，譖潛夫於士英。

translations.literal: Qijie was enraged and slandered Qianfu to Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: Qijie was furious and slandered Qianfu to Ma Shiying.

sentences.zh: 士英怒，冬盡，召潛夫還，以淩駉代。

translations.literal: Shiying was angry; when winter ended he recalled Qianfu and replaced him with Ling Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying was enraged. When winter ended he recalled Qianfu and replaced him with Ling Bing.

sentences.zh: 潛夫亦遭外艱歸。

translations.literal: Qianfu also met with the death of a parent abroad and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu also suffered the death of a parent abroad and returned home.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，給事中林有本疏劾御史彭遇颽，並及潛夫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year, supervising secretary Lin Youben memorialized impeaching censor Peng Yufan, and implicated Qianfu as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year, supervising secretary Lin Youben memorialized to impeach censor Peng Yufan and implicated Qianfu as well.

sentences.zh: 士英以遇颽己私人，置不問，獨令議潛夫罪。

translations.literal: Shiying, because Yufan was his own man, set the matter aside and did not inquire; he ordered only that Qianfu's offense be deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying, because Yufan was his own man, set the matter aside; he ordered deliberation only on Qianfu's offense.

sentences.zh: 先是，有童氏者，自言福王繼妃，廣昌伯劉良佐具禮送之。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been one surnamed Tong who declared herself the Prince of Fu's consort; Earl of Guangchang Liu Liangzuo escorted her with full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a woman surnamed Tong had declared herself the Prince of Fu's consort; the Earl of Guangchang Liu Liangzuo escorted her with full ceremonial honors.

sentences.zh: 潛夫至壽州，見車馬騶從傳呼皇后來，亦稱臣朝謁。

translations.literal: When Qianfu reached Shouzhou and saw horses, outriders, and attendants calling out that the Empress was coming, he too styled himself a subject and paid court homage.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianfu reached Shouzhou and saw horses, outriders, and attendants proclaiming the Empress's arrival, he too styled himself a subject and paid court homage.

sentences.zh: 及童氏入都，王以為假冒，下之獄。

translations.literal: When Tong entered the capital, the Prince judged her a fraud and imprisoned her.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Tong entered the capital, the Prince judged her an impostor and had her imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 遂責潛夫私謁妖婦，逮下獄治之。

translations.literal: He then charged Qianfu with paying private homage to a sorcerous woman, had him arrested and imprisoned, and proceeded against him.
translations.idiomatic: He then charged Qianfu with paying private homage to a fraudulent woman, had him arrested and imprisoned, and proceeded against him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，南都不守，潛夫得脫歸。

translations.literal: Before long the southern capital could not be held; Qianfu escaped and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the southern capital fell; Qianfu managed to escape and return home.

sentences.zh: 聞魯王監國紹興，渡江往謁，命復故官，加太仆少卿，監軍，乃自募三百人列營江上。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Prince of Lu was supervising the realm at Shaoxing, he crossed the river to pay his respects; he was ordered restored to his former office, promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud with duty as supervising officer, and thereupon personally recruited three hundred men and encamped along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Prince of Lu was supervising affairs from Shaoxing, he crossed the river to pay his respects. He was restored to his former office and promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud with military supervision duties; he then personally recruited three hundred men and encamped along the river.

sentences.zh: 尋進大理寺少卿，兼御史如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, retaining his censorial duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review while retaining his censorial duties.

sentences.zh: 順治三年五月晦，江上師盡潰，潛夫走至山陰化龍橋，偕妻妾二孟氏同赴水死，年三十七。

translations.literal: On the last day of the fifth month of the third year of Shunzhi, the river armies were wholly routed; Qianfu fled to Hualong Bridge in Shanyin, and together with his two wives surnamed Meng he drowned himself in the water; he was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the fifth month in the third year of Shunzhi the river garrison collapsed entirely. Qianfu fled to Hualong Bridge in Shanyin and, together with his two wives surnamed Meng, drowned himself in the river. He was thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 始為文逐潛夫者陸培，字鯤庭，舉進士，為行人，奉使事竣歸省。

translations.literal: Lu Pei, who had originally written prose to drive Qianfu away, styled Kunting; he passed the jinshi examinations, served as a courier, and when his mission was complete returned home to visit his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Pei, who had originally written to drive Qianfu away, courtesy name Kunting, passed the jinshi examinations, served as a courier, and after completing his mission returned home to visit his parents.

sentences.zh: 南京既覆，聞潞王又降，以繩授二仆，從容就縊而死，年二十九。

translations.literal: After Nanjing fell, hearing that the Prince of Lu had also surrendered, he gave rope to his two servants and calmly hanged himself; he was twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing fell, on hearing that the Prince of Lu had also surrendered, he gave rope to his two servants and calmly hanged himself. He was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 培少負俊才，有文名，行誼修謹，客華亭，嘗卻奔女於室雲。

translations.literal: In youth Pei possessed outstanding talent and a literary name; his conduct and friendship were strict and careful. While staying as a guest in Huating, he once turned away a fleeing woman who sought refuge in his room.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Lu Pei possessed outstanding talent and literary renown; his conduct was strict and his friendships careful. While lodging in Huating as a guest, he once turned away a fleeing woman who sought refuge in his room.

sentences.zh: 沈廷揚，字季明，崇明人。

translations.literal: Shen Tingyang, styled Jiming, was a man of Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tingyang, courtesy name Jiming, was a native of Chongming.

sentences.zh: 好談經濟。

translations.literal: He loved to discuss statecraft and economic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to discourse on statecraft and practical administration.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，由國子生為內閣中書舍人。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign, through the Imperial Academy he became a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he entered the Imperial Academy and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，帝以山東多警，運道時梗，議復海運。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year the Emperor, because Shandong had many alarms and the transport routes were often blocked, deliberated restoring sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year, with Shandong under frequent alarm and the grain routes often blocked, the Emperor deliberated restoring transport by sea.

sentences.zh: 廷揚生海濱，習水道，上疏極言其便，且輯海運書五卷以呈。

translations.literal: Tingyang was born by the sea and knew the waterways; he memorialized strongly stating its convenience, and moreover compiled a five-volume book on sea transport to present.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyang was born by the sea and knew the waterways well. He memorialized at length on its advantages and compiled a five-volume work on sea transport to present to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，即命造海舟試之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and immediately ordered seagoing vessels built for trial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and at once ordered seagoing vessels built for trial.

sentences.zh: 廷揚乘二舟由淮安出海，抵天津，僅半月。

translations.literal: Tingyang took two boats from Huai'an out to sea and reached Tianjin in only half a month.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyang sailed two vessels from Huai'an out to sea and reached Tianjin in only half a month.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，即加戶部郎中，往登州與巡撫徐人龍計海運事。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly delighted and immediately promoted him to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, sending him to Dengzhou to consult with Grand Coordinator Xu Renlong on sea transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly delighted and promptly promoted him to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, sending him to Dengzhou to consult with Grand Coordinator Xu Renlong on sea transport.

sentences.zh: 初，寧遠軍餉率用天津船，自登州侯東南風，轉粟至天津；

translations.literal: Earlier, Ningyuan army provisions were generally carried on Tianjin ships: from Dengzhou one waited for the southeast wind and transferred grain to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, provisions for the Ningyuan garrison were generally shipped on Tianjin vessels: from Dengzhou one waited for the southeast wind and transferred grain to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 又侯西南風轉至寧遠。

translations.literal: Then one waited for the southwest wind and transferred onward to Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Then one waited for the southwest wind and transferred the grain onward to Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 廷揚請從登州直達寧遠，帝用其議，省費多。

translations.literal: Tingyang requested going directly from Dengzhou to Ningyuan; the Emperor adopted his proposal, and expenses were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyang proposed sailing directly from Dengzhou to Ningyuan; the Emperor adopted his plan, and costs were greatly reduced.

sentences.zh: 十五年命再赴淮安督海運，事竣，加光祿少卿，仍領其事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was ordered again to Huai'an to supervise sea transport; when the task was complete he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, still overseeing the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was again sent to Huai'an to supervise sea transport. When the task was complete he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments while continuing to oversee the operation.

sentences.zh: 及京師陷，福王命廷揚以海舟防江。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, the Prince of Fu ordered Tingyang to defend the river with seagoing vessels.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, the Prince of Fu ordered Tingyang to defend the river with seagoing vessels.

sentences.zh: 尋命兼理餉務，饋江北諸軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was also ordered to manage provisions concurrently and supply the armies north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also charged with managing provisions and supplying the armies north of the river.

sentences.zh: 南京失守，走還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Nanjing fell he fled back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell he fled back to his home district.

sentences.zh: 後航海至舟山，依黃斌卿。

translations.literal: Later he sailed to Zhoushan and relied on Huang Binqing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sailed to Zhoushan and placed himself under Huang Binqing.

sentences.zh: 唐王在福建，授兵部右侍郎，總督水師。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tang, in Fujian, appointed him Right Vice Minister of War with overall command of the navy.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang, holding court in Fujian, appointed him Right Vice Minister of War with overall command of the navy.

sentences.zh: 魯王授官亦如之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu also appointed him to office in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu granted him the same appointment.

sentences.zh: 魯王航海之明年，廷揚督舟師北上，抵福山，次鹿苑。

translations.literal: The year after the Prince of Lu took to sea, Tingyang led the fleet north and reached Fushan, anchoring next at Luyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The year after the Prince of Lu took to sea, Tingyang led the fleet north to Fushan and anchored at Luyuan.

sentences.zh: 夜分颶風大作，舟膠於沙，為大清兵所執。

translations.literal: At midnight a violent hurricane arose; the boats ran aground on sand and were seized by Our Great Qing troops.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight a violent hurricane struck; the vessels ran aground on the shoals and were seized by Our Great Qing forces.

sentences.zh: 諭之降，不從，乃就戮。

translations.literal: They urged him to surrender; he would not agree, and so was executed.
translations.idiomatic: They urged him to surrender; he refused, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 林汝翥，字大葳，福清人。

translations.literal: Lin Ruzhu, styled Dawei, was a man of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Ruzhu, courtesy name Dawei, was a native of Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，授沛縣知縣。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examinations and was appointed magistrate of Pei County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations and was appointed magistrate of Pei County.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，戰卻徐鴻儒兵，緝妖人王普光黨有功，特擢御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he fought off Xu Hongru's troops in battle and suppressed the sorcerer Wang Puguang's faction with merit, and was specially promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he repulsed Xu Hongru's forces in battle and helped suppress the sorcerer Wang Puguang's faction with distinction, earning special promotion to censor.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，巡視京城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, he inspected the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year, he was assigned to inspect the capital.

sentences.zh: 民曹大妻與人奴角口，服毒死。

translations.literal: The wife of Min Cao Da quarreled with another man's slave, took poison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Min Cao Da got into a quarrel with someone else's slave, swallowed poison, and died.

sentences.zh: 火者曹進、傅國興率眾大掠奴主家，用大錐錐其主，刑官不敢問。

translations.literal: The kitchen eunuchs Cao Jin and Fu Guoxing led a crowd in a great pillaging of the slave-owners' household, using large awls to stab their masters, and the judicial officers dared not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The palace cooks Cao Jin and Fu Guoxing led a mob to plunder their masters' homes and stab them with heavy awls, and the penal authorities did not dare to inquire.

sentences.zh: 汝翥捕得進，進懼劾，請受杖，遂杖之五十。

translations.literal: Ruzhu captured Jin; Jin, fearing impeachment, asked to accept the beating, and he was therefore beaten fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhu arrested Jin. Fearing impeachment, Jin asked to take the flogging instead, and Ruzhu had him beaten fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 國興邀於道，罵不已，汝翥收系之，亦請受杖，復杖之。

translations.literal: Guoxing intercepted him on the road and cursed without cease; Ruzhu seized and imprisoned him; he too asked to accept the beating, and Ruzhu beat him again.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxing waylaid him on the road and kept cursing without stop. Ruzhu seized and detained him; he likewise asked to accept the beating, and Ruzhu flogged him again.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢大怒，立傳旨廷杖汝翥。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian flew into a great rage and immediately issued an order for Ruzhu to receive court beatings.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was furious and at once transmitted an imperial order that Ruzhu be beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 先數日，群奄毆殺萬璟。

translations.literal: Several days earlier, a band of eunuchs had beaten Wan Yu to death.
translations.idiomatic: A few days before, a gang of eunuchs had beaten Wan Yu to death.

sentences.zh: 汝翥大懼，逸至遵化。

translations.literal: Ruzhu was greatly afraid and fled to Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhu was terrified and fled to Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄧氵美為代題，都御史孫瑋、御史潘雲翼等交章論救。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Deng Mei submitted a memorial on his behalf; Censor-in-Chief Sun Wei, Censor Pan Yunyi, and others sent successive memorials arguing for his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Deng Mei submitted a memorial on his behalf, and Censor-in-Chief Sun Wei, Censor Pan Yunyi, and others sent one memorial after another pleading for his life.

sentences.zh: 不聽，卒杖之，削籍歸。

translations.literal: The throne would not listen; in the end he was beaten, stripped from the rolls, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not heed them. In the end he was flogged, struck from the register, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起官右參議，分守溫處道，不赴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, he was recalled as Right Assistant Administrator, assigned to guard the Wenzhou-Chuzhou circuit, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled as Right Assistant Administrator to guard the Wenzhou-Chuzhou circuit, but he did not report.

sentences.zh: 久之，起瓊州道，坐奸民煽亂，貶秩歸。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was recalled to the Qiongzhou circuit; for wicked commoners stirring rebellion, his rank was reduced and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled to the Qiongzhou circuit, but when wicked commoners stirred up rebellion he was demoted and sent home.

sentences.zh: 福王時，起雲南僉事，已而解職。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, he was appointed Yunnan Vice Commissioner, but was soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was appointed Vice Commissioner in Yunnan, but was soon removed from office.

sentences.zh: 魯王次長垣，召為兵部右侍郎，與員外郎林惣攻福寧，戰敗被執，諭降不從，系之，吞金屑而死。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu was at Changyuan, he was summoned as Vice Minister of War and, together with department clerk Lin Zong, attacked Funing; defeated in battle and captured, they urged him to surrender but he would not obey; he was imprisoned, swallowed gold dust, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu was at Changyuan, Ruzhu was summoned as Vice Minister of War. Together with department clerk Lin Zong he attacked Funing, was defeated and taken prisoner, and when urged to surrender refused. He was imprisoned, swallowed gold filings, and died.

sentences.zh: 惣，字子野，汝翥同邑人。

translations.literal: Zong, courtesy name Ziye, was a fellow townsman of Ruzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, whose courtesy name was Ziye, came from the same district as Ruzhu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授海寧知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Haining.

sentences.zh: 邑有妖人以劍術惑眾，聚千人，惣捕殺之。

translations.literal: In the district there was a sorcerer who beguiled the crowd with sword magic and gathered a thousand men; Zong captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the county a sorcerer used sword tricks to mislead the people and gathered a thousand followers; Zong captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 南都覆，杭州亦不守，卒乘機乞餉，環署大噪。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital fell and Hangzhou too could not be held, soldiers seized the chance to beg for rations and made a great clamor all around the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: After the Southern Capital fell and Hangzhou too was lost, the troops seized the moment to demand pay and raised a great uproar around the yamen.

sentences.zh: 惣罪為首者，而如其請。

translations.literal: Zong punished the ringleaders, but granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: Zong punished the ringleaders, yet granted what they asked for.

sentences.zh: 以城孤不能存，引去。

translations.literal: Seeing the city isolated and impossible to hold, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the city isolated and impossible to defend, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 唐王以為御史，改文選員外郎，募兵福寧。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince appointed him censor and changed his post to department clerk of Personnel Selection, where he raised troops at Funing.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince made him a censor, then transferred him to department clerk of Personnel Selection and had him raise troops at Funing.

sentences.zh: 聞王被殺，大慟，走匿山中。

translations.literal: When he heard the Prince had been killed, he grieved greatly and fled into hiding in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the Prince had been killed, he grieved deeply and fled into the mountains to hide.

sentences.zh: 及魯王航海至長垣，福清鄉兵請惣為主，與汝翥共攻城，歿於陣。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu sailed the sea and reached Changyuan, Funing local militia asked Zong to lead them; together with Ruzhu he besieged the city and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu put to sea and reached Changyuan, the local militia of Funing asked Zong to lead them. Together with Ruzhu he besieged the city and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 鄭為虹，字天玉，江都人。

translations.literal: Zheng Weihong, courtesy name Tianyu, was a man of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Weihong, styled Tianyu, was a native of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 除浦城知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 唐王道浦城，知其廉，及自立，召為御史。

translations.literal: When the Tang Prince passed through Pucheng, knowing his integrity, upon establishing himself he summoned Weihong as censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang Prince passed through Pucheng he recognized Weihong's integrity, and once he had established his regime he summoned him as censor.

sentences.zh: 部民相率乞留，有十不可去之疏。

translations.literal: The people of the district came in groups begging him to stay, submitting a memorial listing ten reasons he could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the district came in groups to beg him to remain, submitting a memorial listing ten reasons he must not go.

sentences.zh: 乃令以御史巡視仙霞關，駐浦城。

translations.literal: He was therefore ordered to inspect Xianxia Pass as censor, while residing at Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore ordered to inspect Xianxia Pass as censor while remaining stationed at Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 尋令巡撫上遊四府，兼領關務。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to govern the four upstream prefectures and also to take charge of pass affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to govern the four upstream prefectures and to take charge of pass affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 鄭芝龍部將奪民舟，為虹叱責之。

translations.literal: A subordinate general of Zheng Zhilong seized the people's boats; Weihong rebuked and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: A subordinate general of Zheng Zhilong seized the people's boats, and Weihong rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 芝龍訴於王，王為諭解。

translations.literal: Zhilong complained to the Prince, and the Prince interceded on his behalf and settled the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong complained to the Prince, who mediated on his behalf and smoothed the affair over.

sentences.zh: 然是時芝龍已懷異志，盡撤守關將，仙霞嶺二百里間無一人。

translations.literal: Yet by this time Zhilong already harbored rebellious intent and withdrew all the generals guarding the pass; for two hundred li of Xianxia Ridge there was not a single man.
translations.idiomatic: By then, however, Zhilong already nursed treacherous designs and pulled out every general guarding the pass, so that for two hundred li along Xianxia Ridge there was not a single defender.

sentences.zh: 順治三年八月，大清兵長驅直入，為虹亟還浦城，縱士民出走，自守空城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Shunzhi, Our Great Qing troops drove straight in; Weihong hurried back to Pucheng, let officials and commoners flee, and himself held the empty city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Shunzhi, Our Great Qing armies swept in unopposed. Weihong raced back to Pucheng, opened the city so officials and commoners could escape, and alone held the empty town.

sentences.zh: 無何，被執，與給事中黃大鵬並死之，年二十有五。

translations.literal: Before long he was captured and died together with Supervising Secretary Huang Dapeng, aged twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was taken prisoner and died together with Supervising Secretary Huang Dapeng. He was twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 大鵬，字文若，建陽人。

translations.literal: Dapeng, courtesy name Wenruo, was a man of Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dapeng, whose courtesy name was Wenruo, came from Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the thirteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the thirteenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 為義烏知縣，有能聲。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Yiwu and had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yiwu and won a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 唐王召為兵科給事中，從至建寧，令與為虹共守仙霞嶺，竟同死。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince summoned him as supervising secretary of the Military Affairs bureau; he followed to Jianning and was ordered to hold Xianxia Ridge together with Weihong, dying the same death in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince summoned him as supervising secretary of the Military Affairs bureau. He followed the Prince to Jianning and was ordered to hold Xianxia Ridge together with Weihong; in the end they died the same death.

sentences.zh: 時王在延平，聞仙霞關失守，倉猝走汀州。

translations.literal: At this time the Prince was at Yanping; hearing Xianxia Pass had fallen, he fled in haste to Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was then at Yanping. When he heard that Xianxia Pass had fallen, he fled in haste to Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 守延平者為王士和，從走汀州者有胡上琛、熊緯，皆以死事著。

translations.literal: The one defending Yanping was Wang Shihe; those who followed the Prince in flight to Tingzhou included Hu Shangchen and Xiong Wei, all famed for dying in the line of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shihe was left to defend Yanping. Hu Shangchen and Xiong Wei were among those who followed the Prince in flight to Tingzhou; all three became famous for dying in service.

sentences.zh: 士和，字萬育，金溪人。

translations.literal: Shihe, courtesy name Wanyu, was a man of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shihe, styled Wanyu, was a native of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen era he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 南京既覆，江西亦被兵，士和避入閩，授吏部司務。

translations.literal: After Nanjing had fallen and Jiangxi too was overrun, Shihe took refuge in Fujian and was appointed clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing fell and Jiangxi too was overrun by enemy troops, Shihe took refuge in Fujian and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 疏陳時政闕失，凡數千言，唐王刊賜文武諸臣，且召士和入對，嘉獎備至，擢兵部主事。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth the failings of the age at the time, in all several thousand characters; the Tang Prince had it printed and bestowed upon civil and military officials, and also summoned Shihe for audience, praising him to the utmost and promoting him to chief clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on the failings of the times, several thousand characters in all. The Tang Prince had it printed and distributed to civil and military officials, summoned Shihe for an audience, praised him lavishly, and promoted him to chief clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 未一月擢延平知府。

translations.literal: Within a month he was further promoted to prefect of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was promoted again, to prefect of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 八月，王走汀州，留兵部侍郎曹覆泰偕士和居守。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, when the Prince fled to Tingzhou, he left Vice Minister of War Cao Futai together with Shihe to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, when the Prince fled to Tingzhou, he left Vice Minister of War Cao Futai together with Shihe to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 俄警報疊至，士和召父老曰：「吾雖一月郡守，當與城存亡。

translations.literal: Before long alarm after alarm arrived; Shihe summoned the elders and said: "Though I have been prefect for only a month, I shall live and die with the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long alarm after alarm arrived. Shihe summoned the elders and said, "Though I have been prefect barely a month, I will live and die with this city.

sentences.zh: 若等可速出，毋使數萬生靈盡膏斧锧。」

translations.literal: You should leave quickly; do not let tens of thousands of living souls all be ground beneath axe and cleaver.
translations.idiomatic: Leave at once, all of you—do not let tens of thousands of lives be ground beneath axe and cleaver.

sentences.zh: 眾泣，士和亦泣。

translations.literal: The crowd wept, and Shihe wept too.
translations.idiomatic: The people wept, and Shihe wept with them.

sentences.zh: 退入內署，謂友人曰：「吾一介書生，數月而忝二千石，安敢偷生。」

translations.literal: Retiring to the inner office, he said to a friend: "I am but a single scholar; in a few months I have been honored with a two-thousand-dan post—how dare I steal life?"
translations.idiomatic: Retiring to the inner office, he said to a friend, "I am only an obscure scholar who in a few months was honored with a two-thousand-dan post—how dare I cling to life?"

sentences.zh: 其友勸止之，正色曰：「君子愛人以德，姑息何為。」

translations.literal: His friend urged him to stop; he said sternly: "The noble man loves men through virtue—what is indulgence for?"
translations.idiomatic: His friend tried to dissuade him. He said sternly, "A gentleman loves others through virtue—what is the use of false comfort?"

sentences.zh: 從容正衣冠，閉戶投繯死。

translations.literal: Composed, he straightened cap and robes, shut the door, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Composed, he straightened his cap and robes, shut the door, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 上琛，字席公。

translations.literal: Shangchen, courtesy name Xigong.
translations.idiomatic: Shangchen, whose courtesy name was Xigong.

sentences.zh: 世襲福州右衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Hereditary commander of the Fuzhou Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He held the hereditary post of commander of the Fuzhou Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，能詩。

translations.literal: Fond of reading and able to compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and could write poetry.

sentences.zh: 既襲職，復舉武鄉試。

translations.literal: Having inherited his office, he again passed the military provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: After inheriting his post he also passed the military provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 唐王時，官錦衣衛指揮，遷署都督僉事，充禦營總兵官，從至汀州。

translations.literal: Under the Tang Prince he served as commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, moved to acting Regional Commander, and filled the post of general commanding the Imperial Guard camp, following the Prince to Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang Prince he served as commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was transferred to acting Regional Commander, and was made general commanding the Imperial Guard camp, accompanying the Prince to Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王被執，上琛奔還福州，謂家人曰：「吾世臣，不可茍活，為我采毒草來。」

translations.literal: When the Prince was captured, Shangchen fled back to Fuzhou and said to his family: "I am a hereditary minister—I cannot live shamefully; gather poison plants for me."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince was taken, Shangchen fled back to Fuzhou and told his family, "I am a hereditary minister—I cannot live in disgrace. Bring me poison herbs."

sentences.zh: 妾劉年二十，願同死。

translations.literal: His concubine Liu, aged twenty, wished to die together with him.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine Liu, aged twenty, asked to die with him.

sentences.zh: 上琛喜曰：「汝幼婦亦能死耶！」

translations.literal: Shangchen rejoiced and said: "You, a young wife, can also die!"
translations.idiomatic: Shangchen was delighted and said, "Even you, a young wife, are willing to die!"

sentences.zh: 遂整冠帶與妾共飲藥酒而卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon they straightened caps and sashes and together drank medicinal wine and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then they straightened their caps and sashes, drank poisoned wine together, and died.

sentences.zh: 緯，字文江，南昌人。

translations.literal: Wei, courtesy name Wenjiang, was a man of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, styled Wenjiang, was a native of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: Appointed as courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier.

sentences.zh: 兩京既覆，每飲酒，輒涕泗交橫下。

translations.literal: After both capitals had fallen, whenever he drank wine tears would stream down together.
translations.idiomatic: After both capitals had fallen, whenever he drank wine tears would pour down his face.

sentences.zh: 友人語之曰：「昔狼覃有言『吾未獲死所』，子既有誌，曷求所乎？」

translations.literal: A friend said to him: "Long ago Lang Tan had a saying: 'I have not yet found the place to die.' You already have the will—why not seek such a place?"
translations.idiomatic: A friend said to him, "Long ago Lang Tan said, 'I have not yet found where to die.' You already have the will—why not go find that place?"

sentences.zh: 乃赴延平謁唐王，擢給事中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Yanping to pay court to the Tang Prince and was promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he went to Yanping to pay court to the Tang Prince and was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋扈行至汀州，遘變，從官皆散，緯仍奔赴。

translations.literal: Soon he followed on the journey to Tingzhou; when disaster struck, the accompanying officials all dispersed, but Wei still pressed forward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed the Prince on the road to Tingzhou. When disaster struck, the officials in attendance all scattered, but Wei pressed on.

sentences.zh: 遇大清兵，死之。

translations.literal: He encountered Our Great Qing troops and died.
translations.idiomatic: He ran into Our Great Qing troops and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：廢興之故，豈非天道哉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The causes of rise and fall—are they not Heaven's way?
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Are the causes of rise and fall not the way of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 金聲等以烏合之師，張皇奮呼，欲挽明祚於已廢之後，心離勢渙，敗不旋踵，何尺寸之能補。

translations.literal: Jin Sheng and the rest, with a mob-gathered army, stretched their banners and shouted in frenzy, wishing to pull back the Ming dynasty's mandate after it had already fallen; hearts were sundered and their strength scattered—they were defeated in no time. What capacity did they have to mend it by even an inch?
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng and his fellows, with a hastily gathered rabble, raised banners and shouted themselves hoarse, trying to restore the Ming mandate after it had already collapsed. Hearts were divided and their force dissipated; defeat came almost at once. What could they have mended, even by an inch?

sentences.zh: 然卒能致命遂誌，視死如歸，事雖無成，亦存其誌而已矣。

translations.literal: Yet in the end they could give their lives to fulfill their resolve, facing death as returning home; though the undertaking came to nothing, they preserved their purpose—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end they gave their lives to fulfill their resolve, facing death as if returning home. Though their cause came to nothing, they kept their purpose—and that is enough.
